# LeadFlow Sentinel

[![CI](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel?display_name=tag)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel/releases)
[![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%20%7C%203.11%20%7C%203.12-blue)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel/blob/main/pyproject.toml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE)
[![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-101%20passing-brightgreen)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel/tree/main/tests)

**Read-only CRM health, lead-to-booking monitoring and revenue-leakage detection for GoHighLevel (HighLevel) agencies.**

LeadFlow Sentinel audits a GoHighLevel sub-account snapshot, scores its health, and reports the exact leads, opportunities and bookings where money is leaking — with the evidence attached, not a vague "your CRM could be better".

- Zero-dependency Python core. No account, no API key, no dashboard needed to get a first report.
- Read-only by design: nothing in the CRM is created, updated or deleted.
- Deterministic: the same snapshot always produces the same score, so numbers in a client proposal cannot drift overnight.
- AI is optional and fenced: narratives are only accepted when every claim traces back to a finding.

```bash
python -m leadflow_sentinel demo --out demo-audit.json
```

That writes a full audit of a synthetic agency account (52 contacts, 24 opportunities, 15 webhook events, 12 planted defect classes) in under a second.

---

## Why this exists

GoHighLevel agencies do not lose money because a dashboard is missing. They lose it because:

1. **Leads arrive and nobody follows up.** A form fill creates a contact; no opportunity, no call, no appointment. The lead goes cold inside 72 hours.
2. **The same person exists three times.** One record from a Facebook lead form, one from a website form, one imported from a spreadsheet. Reporting counts them as three leads; the follow-up automation fires on the wrong one.
3. **Bookings are never confirmed.** An appointment sits in `pending` forever; the show-up rate collapses and nobody notices until the month ends.
4. **Webhooks fail silently.** HighLevel retries, times out or pauses a subscription; the workflow that was supposed to run simply did not run.

Each of those is measurable from data the account already holds. LeadFlow Sentinel measures them, prices them in severity, and tells the operator which specific records to fix first.

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/leadflow-sentinel
cd leadflow-sentinel

# 1. Prove the detectors fire on known planted defects
python -m leadflow_sentinel selftest

# 2. Audit the synthetic demo account, write a JSON report
python -m leadflow_sentinel demo --out demo-audit.json

# 3. Audit the demo account and write a client-ready Markdown report
python -m leadflow_sentinel demo --out demo-audit.md

# 4. Audit your own snapshot (see docs/GHL-INTEGRATION.md for the shape)
python -m leadflow_sentinel audit --dataset s

| Duplicate clusters | Identity clusters with the match basis (email / phone / name) and confidence |
| Journey stats | Leads, opportunities, bookings, follow-ups and the measured booking rate against target |
| Integration stats | Duplicate webhook deliveries and failed events |
| Data completeness | Events received vs used vs rejected, with reasons — a partial picture is never read as a complete one |
| Root-cause notes | Optional, evidence-linked (see `--ai`) |

## Scoring model

The overall score is a weighted average of four components. Weights are configuration, not constants.

| Component | Default weight | Measures |
|---|---:|---|
| Data quality | 0.45 | Missing/invalid emails and phones, missing names and sources, duplicate clusters |
| Pipeline | 0.22 | Orphaned opportunities, missing stages, stalled deals, won deals without an appointment |
| Journey | 0.23 | Lead → opportunity → booking → follow-up conversion inside configured windows |
| Integration | 0.10 | Duplicate deliveries and failed webhook events |

Weights renormalise automatically when a component has no data (an account with no webhook subscriptions should not be punished for a missing integration score). Every excluded component is named in `score.excluded` with the reason and the weight it gave up, and `score_explanation` prints the arithmetic so the total can be recomputed by hand. See [docs/TRUST-MODEL.md](docs/TRUST-MODEL.md).

Grade bands: `A ≥ 90`, `B ≥ 80`, `C ≥ 70`, `D ≥ 55`, `F < 55`.

Per-subject penalty: the worst finding dominates and every additional finding adds a quarter of its own penalty, capped at 100 — one seriously broken record is not diluted by fifty healthy ones, but a record with five problems still scores worse than one with a single problem.

## Rule catalogue

20 rules across four categories, all 20 live. `INT-003` is the one that exists to catch the tool's own blind spot: an integration that stops sending webhooks looks identical to a healthy funnel unless the silence is measured (see `docs/TRUST-MODEL.md`).

| Rule | Severity | Category | Checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| DQ-001 | medium | data quality | Missing email |
| DQ-002 | high | data quality | Invalid email format |
| DQ-003 | medium | data quality | Missing phone |
| DQ-004 | high | data quality | Invalid phone number |
| DQ-005 | low | data quality | Missing contact name |
| DQ-006 | low | data quality | Missing lead source |
| DQ-007 | low | data quality | Non-canonical phone format |
| DQ-008 | high | data quality | Duplicate contact cluster |
| OPP-001 | high | pipeline | Orphaned opportunity (contact no longer exists) |
| OPP-002 | medium | pipeline | Opportunity missing stage |
| OPP-003 | medium | pipeline | Stalled opportunity (no update in N days) |
| OPP-004 | medium | pipeline | Won deal without an appointment |
| JRN-001 | high | journey | Contact created without an opportunity |
| JRN-002 | high | journey | Appointment not confirmed |
| JRN-003 | medium | journey | Booked appointment without an opportunity |
| JRN-004 | medium | journey | Lead without recorded follow-up |
| JRN-005 | high | journey | Lead past booking window with no appointment |
| INT-001 | medium | integration | Duplicate webhook deliveries |
| INT-002 | high | integration | Event processing failure |
| INT-003 | high | integration | Missing expected event — expected types absent, recent contacts with no event, low event-to-contact link rate |

Every threshold behind these rules is configurable — default country code, stale-opportunity window, booking window, confirm window, follow-up window, target booking rate, which rules run, and per-rule severity overrides.

## Configuration

Set `LEADFLOW_CONFIG` to either a JSON file path or an inline JSON object:

```json
{
  "default_country_code": "92",
  "stale_opportunity_days": 14,
  "thresholds": {
    "opportunity_within_hours": 24,
    "appointment_confirm_within_hours": 48,
    "first_followup_within_hours": 24,
    "no_booking_within_hours": 72,
    "target_booking_rate": 0.2
  },
  "weights": { "data_quality": 0.45, "pipeline": 0.22, "journey": 0.23, "integration": 0.10 },
  "enabled_rules": ["DQ-001", "DQ-002", "DQ-008", "OPP-001"],
  "severity_overrides": { "DQ-003": "low" },
  "event_window_days": 30,
  "expected_event_types": ["contact.created", "opportunity.created", "appointment.created"]
}
```

A med spa and a roofing contractor do not share a funnel. The thresholds above are starting points, not truth; the config is how an agency encodes its own SLA.

## HTTP API

```bash
python -m leadflow_sentinel serve --port 8080
```

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/health` | Liveness and version |
| GET | `/v1/rules` | Full rule catalogue with severities |
| POST | `/v1/audit` | Audit a posted snapshot for one location |
| POST | `/v1/audit/demo` | Audit the synthetic demo account |
| POST | `/v1/webhooks/ghl` | Idempotent GoHighLevel webhook receiver |
| GET | `/v1/events` | Recent stored events (status, attempts, duplicates) |
| POST | `/v1/events/{delivery_id}/retry` | Replay a failed delivery |
| GET | `/v1/metrics` | Counters for scrapers and dashboards |
| GET | `/v1/diagnostics` | What this instance runs: version, redacted config, available narrative engines, per-location event counters |
| POST | `/v1/report` | Render a Markdown report for a posted snapshot |

Multi-tenant isolation is enforced at the edge: every business endpoint requires an `X-Location-Id` header, and a body that disagrees with it is rejected with `403`. The API is *dataset-in, not credential-in* — it never stores GoHighLevel private integration tokens.

## AI root-cause notes (optional)

```bash
python -m leadflow_sentinel demo --out demo-ai.md --ai
```

Default provider is a deterministic template provider: no network, no key, fully reproducible. Set `GEMINI_API_KEY` (plus optional `LEADFLOW_AI_MODEL`) to use Gemini, or `LEADFLOW_AI_DISABLED=1` to force templates.

The guardrail is the point: a narrative is only accepted if every `finding_id` it references exists, every number it states appears in that finding's evidence, and it lands no claim the detector did not make. Rejected narratives are kept in the payload under `rejected` with the reason — the refusal is auditable too.

## Development

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev,api]"
pytest -q                    # 101 tests, no network, no fixtures on disk
ruff check src tests
ruff format --check src tests
python -m leadflow_sentinel selftest
```

CI runs the suite on Ubuntu and Windows across Python 3.10 and 3.12, plus lint, format and a demo-audit smoke test.

Tests use a synthetic dataset only. No customer data, ever.

# ghl-automation-engine

HighLevel (GoHighLevel) integration engine for teams that put automations in
production and cannot afford them to be quietly wrong.

The GoHighLevel ecosystem already has a 900-tool MCP server. Tool *count* is not
the bottleneck. Reliability is. This project is deliberately narrow: it makes the
failure modes visible instead of silent.

## The four failures this exists to prevent

| Failure | What it looks like in production | What this library does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Silent pagination truncation | Page 2 of 5 fails, the caller returns page 1, a downstream workflow treats 100 contacts as "all contacts" and archives the rest | Cursor walking is exhaustive by contract: you get a `Collection` with an honest `complete` flag, or a `GhlPartialResultError` carrying what was collected |
| Refresh-token stampede | 12 concurrent workers see an expired token, all refresh, the provider rotates the refresh token, 11 calls return `invalid_grant`, the integration hard-fails | Single-flight refresh under a lock with a double-checked expiry, and the rotated token is persisted before the lock is released |
| PII in logs | A debug line logs the contact upsert body and every email address lands in the log aggregator | Recursive redaction of credentials, emails, and phone numbers before any log record is emitted |
| Untestable integrations | Every test needs a live sub-account and a private token, so there are no tests | An offline mock server with fault injection; the whole suite runs on a clean machine in seconds |
| Webhook replays processed twice | A captured delivery is resent, or a platform retry arrives after a partial write, and the contact is created or the invoice is paid twice | Signature + timestamp window + an atomic seen-set; a duplicate returns `200` with `process=false`, so the sender stops retrying and your code does not run again |

## Install

```bash
git clone <this repo>
cd ghl-automation-engine
python -m pytest
```

No dependencies. The runtime uses only the standard library, so `pytest` is the
only thing you need, and CI needs no Docker and no network.

## Quickstart

```python
from ghl_client import ContactsResource, GhlClient, PrivateIntegrationToken

client = GhlClient(
    PrivateIntegrationToken(token="pit-..."),
    location_id="loc_...",
)

contacts = ContactsResource(client)
result = contacts.search(query="@example.com")

if not result.complete:
    raise SystemExit(f"refusing to act on {len(result)} of an unknown total")

for contact in result.items:
    ...
```

Idempotent writes:

```python
# Replaying this call does not create a duplicate contact.
contacts.upsert({"email": "jane@example.com"}, idempotency_key="sync-run-2026-11-21")
```

## Webhooks

```python
from ghl_webhooks import Receiver

receiver = Receiver(["whsec_..."])

def handle_delivery(headers, raw_body):
    intake = receiver.handle(headers, raw_body)
    if intake.should_process:
        dispatch(intake.event)      # a real, first-time, verified event
    return intake.http_status, {"status": intake.status.value}
```

| PII in logs | A debug line logs the contact upsert body and every email address lands in the log aggregator | Recursive redaction of credentials, emails, and phone numbers before any log record is emitted |
| Untestable integrations | Every test needs a live sub-account and a private token, so there are no tests | An offline mock server with fault injection; the whole suite runs on a clean machine in seconds |
| Webhook replays processed twice | A captured delivery is resent, or a platform retry arrives after a partial write, and the contact is created or the invoice is paid twice | Signature + timestamp window + an atomic seen-set; a duplicate returns `200` with `process=false`, so the sender stops retrying and your code does not run again |

## Install

```bash
git clone <this repo>
cd ghl-automation-engine
python -m pytest
```

No dependencies. The runtime uses only the standard library, so `pytest` is the
only thing you need, and CI needs no Docker and no network.

## Quickstart

```python
from ghl_client import ContactsResource, GhlClient, PrivateIntegrationToken

client = GhlClient(
    PrivateIntegrationToken(token="pit-..."),
    location_id="loc_...",
)

contacts = ContactsResource(client)
result = contacts.search(query="@example.com")

if not result.complete:
    raise SystemExit(f"refusing to act on {len(result)} of an unknown total")

for contact in result.items:
    ...
```

Idempotent writes:

```python
# Replaying this call does not create a duplicate contact.
contacts.upsert({"email": "jane@example.com"}, idempotency_key="sync-run-2026-11-21")
```

## Webhooks

```python
from ghl_webhooks import Receiver

receiver = Receiver(["whsec_..."])

def handle_delivery(headers, raw_body):
    intake = receiver.handle(headers, raw_body)
    if intake.should_process:
        dispatch(intake.event)      # a real, first-time, verified event
    return intake.http_status, {"status": intake.status.value}
```

Three things this does that a naive handler does not:

* **Order matters.** Nothing is parsed until the signature verifies, and no event id is
  claimed until every other check has passed — so an attacker cannot burn event ids to
  block genuine deliveries.
* **Duplicates are visible.** A repeat delivery answers `200` with `process=false`. The
  sender stops retrying; your application does not re-run. "Received" and "acted on" are
  different questions and both get an answer.
* **Unknown event types are kept.** An unrecognised type is delivered with
  `event.is_known == False` and its raw body intact. Silently discarding it is how an
  integration appears healthy while ingesting nothing.

Signature framing (header names, hex vs base64, what exactly is signed) is configuration
rather than a guess, because getting it wrong silently rejects real traffic. See
`docs/adr/ADR-002-webhook-signature-framing.md` for the default assumption and how to
confirm it against one captured delivery.

Run the intake demo — no network, no credentials:

```bash
python examples/demo_webhooks.py
```

## Governed MCP server

```bash
export GHL_PIT_TOKEN=pit-...      export GHL_LOCATION_ID=loc_...
export GHL_MCP_MODE=read-write    # default is read-only
export GHL_MCP_APPROVAL_SECRET=... # required before any write will run
ghl-mcp                            # JSON-RPC over stdio
```

Five tools: `get_contact`, `search_contacts`, `upsert_contact`, `rate_limit_status`,
`server_governance`. Scope is narrow on purpose — a tool that returns a plausible empty
result is worse than a tool that is absent, so the unimplemented ones are listed with
reasons instead of being faked.

The part that matters is the interceptor every call passes through, in this order:

1. **Mode.** Read-only unless the operator turned writes on. A refusal is `read_only_mode`,
   never a `200` with an empty body.
2. **Schema.** Unknown properties are rejected, so there is no `locationId` to argue about —
   cross-account access is not a policy, it is a shape that does not exist.
3. **Location.** The server is bound to one sub-account; an unbound client gets
   `cross_location` rather than a default location.
4. **Approval.** A write needs a single-use, short-lived token issued for *that tool and
   those exact arguments*. A token for one contact cannot be spent on another.
5. **Budget.** Session ceilings stop a loop before the platform rate limiter or the invoice
   does.

```bash
# the human approves one specific change
ghl-mcp approve --tool upsert_contact \
  --args '{"email":"ada@example.com","first_name":"Ada"}'
```

`upsert_contact` also takes `dry_run: true`, which returns the payload it *would* send and
touches nothing. `server_governance` reports the active policy, the PII allowlist, and the
blocked-tool list. Without `GHL_PIT_TOKEN` the server exits `2` and says why, instead of
starting up to answer 401s that an agent would narrate as "no contacts found".

Full detail: [`docs/MCP.md`](docs/MCP.md).

## Offline development

```bash
python -m ghl_mock --port 8080
python examples/demo_offline.py     # full round trip against the mock
```

The mock can be told to fail on purpose, which is the point:

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:8080/__admin/inject \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"path": "/contacts/search", "status": 429, "times": 1, "retry_after": "2"}'
```

## Architecture

```
src/ghl_client/
  errors.py       typed hierarchy; retryable is a property of the error, not the caller
  ratelimit.py    sliding-window budget, 90 req / 10 s (platform allows 100)
  retry.py        Retry-After (seconds and HTTP-date), capped at 120 s, full jitter
  transport.py    the only module that touches a socket; injectable
  auth.py         private tokens + OAuth with single-flight refresh and persistence
  pagination.py   exhaustive cursor walking with loop detection
  client.py       versioning, budgeting, redaction, request ids
  resources/      contacts (search, idempotent upsert)
src/ghl_mock/
  store.py        in-memory contacts with email/phone dedupe and cursor paging
  app.py          stdlib HTTP server + fault injection admin endpoints
src/ghl_mcp/
  server.py       JSON-RPC over stdio; call_tool is the only path to a handler
  governance.py   mode, approval tokens bound to arguments, session budget, location guard
  tools.py        five tools, each declaring scope, risk, endpoint and dry-run support
  registry.py     tool specs; carries requires_location per tool
  schema.py       strict JSON Schema subset: unknown keywords raise instead of being ignored
  projection.py   PII allowlist and field truncation for anything a model will read
  audit.py        one JSON line per call: digests, decision, duration — never the arguments
src/ghl_webhooks/
  signature.py    HMAC verification; header/encoding/prefix/signed-payload are configuration
  replay.py       timestamp window + atomic seen-set behind a one-method store protocol
  events.py       event parsing that preserves unknown types instead of dropping them
  receiver.py     ordered intake: size -> signature -> timestamp -> parse -> claim
src/ghl_attribution/
  mapping.py      required field keys, live id binding, drift as a startup error
  events.py       webhook body -> touch; "no campaign signal" is a first-class answer
  policy.py       which fields may be written: blanks + activity time, credit preserved
  ledger.py       event claim store (in-process default, protocol for a durable one)
  engine.py       discovery -> claim -> compare -> upsert; dry run returns the delta
```

Design decisions worth defending:

* **Mock before client.** The contract is written down as executable mock behaviour
  first, so the client is developed against a specification rather than against
  whatever the live API happened to return at 3 a.m.
* **Errors carry context.** Status, method, path, request id, and location id are
  attached at the point of failure, so a support ticket does not need a repro.
* **No dependency on the platform's SDK.** The SDK pulls its own HTTP stack and
  its own opinions about retries; both would fight with the retry and budget logic
  above.
* **A dropped connection is a dataset, not a surprise.** `urllib` wraps neither
  `ECONNRESET` nor Windows' `WSAECONNABORTED`, so the transport types them itself: every
  socket-level failure becomes a retryable `GhlTransportError` instead of a bare `OSError`
  that a calling workflow has no reason to handle.

## Attribution engine

The server is only half of it: leads arrive from forms, quizzes, and landing
pages, and the reason to send them to GoHighLevel is attribution. `ghl_attribution`
does that without the two failure modes that make attribution worthless — a lead
re-credited on every later visit, and one lead in the CRM three times over.

```python
from ghl_attribution import AttributionEngine

engine = AttributionEngine(client)                 # resolves custom field ids at startup
result = engine.ingest({                            # webhook body, verbatim
    "event_id": "evt-9f2",
    "email": "lead@example.com",
    "utm_source": "google",
    "utm_medium": "cpc",
    "utm_campaign": "spring",
    "occurred_at": "2026-11-20T10:00:00Z",
})
result.status        # IngestStatus.APPLIED
result.applied       # ("utm_source", "utm_medium", "utm_campaign", "first_touch_at", "last_touch_at")
```

* **Credit is append-only.** A later touch from another source advances
  `last_touch_at` and nothing else. `utm_source=direct` from a returning lead
  cannot erase the campaign that paid for them.
* **Two idempotency layers.** The event claim stops a redelivered webhook, the
  client's upsert ledger stops a duplicate contact after a failed retry, and the
  claim is released on failure so a retry is the same operation.
* **Refuses to start on schema drift.** Missing, retyped, or duplicated custom
  fields raise `AttributionMappingError` with every problem listed — before the
  first write, not after the reports break.
* `dry_run=True` returns the exact field payload without writing.

Full detail, including the required field keys: [docs/ATTRIBUTION.md](docs/ATTRIBUTION.md).

A worked case runs offline — seven relay deliveries (two of them redeliveries), a
later touch, a direct revisit, a dry run, and a mid-flight schema drift:

```bash
python examples/case_lead_attribution.py
```

It ends with two contacts, the paid-search credit intact, and the drift refused
before the first write. Write-up: [docs/CASE-STUDY-ATTRIBUTION.md](docs/CASE-STUDY-ATTRIBUTION.md)
— figures that need a real deployment are marked `TBD`, not guessed.

## Conversation triage

`ghl_triage` starts where a messaging bot usually goes wrong: it decides **what
kind of message this is and whether a human must take it**, before anything is
drafted. Eight intents, and every one of them states what it is *not*.

```python
from ghl_triage import Intent, Entity, decide

plan = decide(
    Intent.APPOINTMENT,
    0.93,
    text="Can we move it to later next week?",
    present_entities=[],          # no date was given
)
plan.escalate        # True
plan.queue           # 'human_review'
plan.reasons         # (EscalationReason.MISSING_ENTITY,)
plan.auto_reply_allowed   # False — always, even when the message is clean
```

Escalation reasons, in fixed precedence: `classifier_error`, `empty_message`,
`human_only_intent` (billing / opt-out / unclear), `human_requested`,
`missing_entity`, `low_confidence` (below `0.55`), `repeated_contact` (3+ in a
thread), `already_escalated`. Classification that fails at all goes through
`fail_closed()`, which can only report `classifier_error` or `empty_message` —
a failure is never dressed up as a confident routing decision.

Taxonomy, the full escalation table and the failure contract:
[docs/TRIAGE.md](docs/TRIAGE.md).

## Reporting warehouse

`ghl_warehouse` answers the question a sync usually gets wrong: **what happens when
the same data arrives twice?** Nothing — a payload whose tracked attributes hash to
the current version is not a new version, so the dimension records change instead of
polling frequency.

```python
from ghl_warehouse import (
    InMemoryWarehouse, JsonFileWatermarkStore, IncrementalContactExtractor,
)

extractor = IncrementalContactExtractor(
    contacts_resource, InMemoryWarehouse(), JsonFileWatermarkStore("state/watermarks.json")
)

plan = extractor.run(dry_run=True)   # no writes, mark untouched
stats = extractor.run()              # load, then advance
stats.new_versions, stats.unchanged, stats.pages
```

The same contract carries the **opportunity grain**: one type-2 fact per deal, where a
stage move is a new version and the previous row is closed at the observed timestamp.
`InMemoryOpportunityWarehouse.open_value()` sums current open deals only, so a funnel
number has one definition. Unknown statuses and non-numeric `monetaryValue` are
rejected rather than coerced — a load that fails loudly beats a funnel that grows an
"other" bar.

The load order is the design: read the mark, walk every page (a partial walk raises
`IncompleteExtractError` and loads nothing), load rows, and only then advance the
mark — as far as what was *loaded*, never what was *seen*. Watermarks are monotonic
and reads are overlapped by 300s, because commits do not arrive in timestamp order.

Schema, load rules, failure table and the client-side cost disclaimer:
[docs/REPORTING.md](docs/REPORTING.md).

## Status

Built and tested:

* typed errors, sliding-window rate budget, retry with `Retry-After`
* OAuth single-flight refresh with file persistence
* exhaustive cursor pagination with partial-result signalling
* contacts search and idempotent upsert
* offline mock server with fault injection (429 / 5xx / auth rejection)
* webhook intake: HMAC verification, timestamp window, replay seen-set, unknown-type preservation
* governed MCP server: read-only default, argument-bound single-use approvals, `dry_run`,
  location guard, session budget, digest-only audit log, blocked tools declared not faked
* attribution engine: append-only first-touch credit, event claim + upsert ledger,
  custom-field discovery with drift refusal, dry-run plans
* attribution case study: reproducible demo + page, invariants pinned by tests
* conversation triage: 8-intent taxonomy with stated exclusions, escalation policy
  with recorded reasons and fixed precedence, fail-closed classification,
  drafts-only by construction (`auto_reply_allowed` is never true)
* reporting warehouse: star schema validated at import, type-2 contact dimension
  keyed on a payload hash, monotonic watermarks advanced only after a load,
  interrupted and replayed runs proven idempotent by tests
* opportunity fact at deal grain: stage moves versioned, stale payloads ignored,
  open value defined once, mock endpoints for `/opportunities` covered end to end
* durable warehouse sink: `SqliteWarehouse` keeps the reference sink's contract in a file, one transaction per record, one current row per key enforced by index, and a manifest whose digest is reproducible for identical data
* snapshot CLI: `ghl-snapshot write` records the warehouse manifest to a file, `ghl-snapshot diff` exits 1 on any difference, and identical data produces byte-identical snapshots
* 377 tests, no network, no credentials
* `python examples/demo_snapshot.py` shows identical loads producing byte-identical snapshots

Not built yet, on purpose — in this order:

1. live smoke tests behind an opt-in environment flag
2. durable replay store adapter (Redis/Postgres) beyond the in-process default
3. multi-touch weighting (first touch is the only model implemented today)
4. the triage classifier and its labelled evaluation set (GHL-023 / GHL-024) —
   until that harness reports accuracy, cost and latency, no accuracy number is
   quoted for triage anywhere
5. conversation / attribution facts and a durable SQL sink for the warehouse
   (GHL-027); contacts and opportunities are the two grains today, and the
   in-memory sinks are reference implementations, not storage

# GHL DevOps Toolkit ### The Open-Source Developer Platform for GoHighLevel Automations [![CI](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/ghl-devops-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/ghl-devops-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Tests Passing](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tests-20%2F20%20Passing-emerald.svg?style=flat-square)](QA_REPORT.md) [![TypeScript 5](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.0-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) [![Next.js 16](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-16.4-black.svg?style=flat-square)](https://nextjs.org/) [![Prisma 6](https://img.shields.io/badge/Prisma-6.x-2D3748.svg?style=flat-square)](https://www.prisma.io/) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![WhatsApp Support](https://img.shields.io/badge/WhatsApp-Contact%20Engineer-25D366?style=flat-square&logo=whatsapp&logoColor=white)](https://wa.me/923167417135)

Inspect APIs · Debug Webhooks · Simulate Workflows · Execute Automated Regression Tests · Validate Snapshots · Diagnose Integrations with AI

[Quick Start](#-quick-start) • [Core Modules](#-core-modules) • [Architecture](#-system-architecture) • [Automated QA](#-automated-testing--qa) • [Security](#-security--compliance) • [Direct WhatsApp Support](#-contact--engineering-inquiries) ---
## 📌 Overview **GHL DevOps Toolkit** is an open-source engineering platform built specifically for **GoHighLevel (GHL) developers, AI automation engineers, and CRM technical architects**. Building and deploying mission-critical GoHighLevel workflows often requires complex webhook debugging, rate-limit management, snapshot migration testing, and manual scenario execution. **GHL DevOps Toolkit** bridges this gap by providing an integrated, production-grade developer environment that replaces guesswork with deterministic testing, deep observability, and AI-assisted troubleshooting. Whether you are building high-volume marketplace apps, setting up multi-location SaaS snapshots, or orchestrating AI voice and messaging agents, this toolkit equips you with the tooling you need. --- ## 🚀 Key Features ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ GHL DEVOPS TOOLKIT SUITE │ ├──────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┤ │ 🔌 API Explorer │ 🪝 Webhook Inspector │ ⚡ Workflow Simulator │ │ Test live & demo │ Ingest & replay │ Simulate lead journeys │ │ GHL v2 endpoints │ events with HMAC │ without firing live triggers │ ├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┤ │ 🧪 Test Engine │ 📦 Snapshot Checker │ 🤖 AI Debugger │ │ Automated regression │ Validate structure, │ Explain API errors & │ │ & assertion suites │ duplicates & schemas │ diagnose payload failures with AI │ ├──────────────────────┴──────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────┤ │ 📊 Integration Monitor · Health checks, latency percentiles & alerts │ │ 📑 Report Generator · Export audits in HTML, PDF, CSV, and JSON │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` - **GHL API Explorer**: Execute and manage requests against HighLevel API endpoints (`/contacts`, `/opportunities`, `/calendars`, `/locations`, `/users`). View formatted JSON, response headers, status codes, latency, and saved request history. - **Webhook Inspector**: Generate unique webhook capture slugs, inspect raw and parsed payloads in real-time, filter by event type, and safely replay events with HMAC-SHA256 signature verification. - **Workflow Simulator**: Step-by-step lead journey simulator (new lead, stage change, appointment booked/cancelled, form submission). Test logic branches with zero risk of accidentally triggering real automations inside customer sub-accounts. - **Automation Testing Engine**: Define test cases with declarative assertions (`equals`, `contains`, `exists`, `not_null`, `greater_than`, `less_than`). Group tests into suites and run automated regression passes with structured failure reporting. - **Snapshot Validator**: Upload and analyze GoHighLevel snapshot JSON exports. Detects missing configurations, broken pipeline/calendar references, duplicate workflows, and version incompatibilities before importing into live locations. - **AI Debugger**: Context-aware AI diagnostic engine powered by Google Gemini and OpenRouter models. Translates cryptic GHL 400/401/403/429 errors into actionable fixes and generates corrected API payloads. - **Integration Monitor**: Proactive health-checking engine that pings GHL connections, monitors response time percentiles, tracks failure rates, and fires threshold alerts. - **Multi-Format Technical Reports**: Export comprehensive audit reports in HTML, JSON, and CSV covering API diagnostics, webhook receipts, test matrices, and system health. --- ## 🛠️ Technology Stack | Layer | Technologies | | :--- | :--- | | **Frontend Framework** | [Next.js 16](https://nextjs.org/) (App Router), [React 19](https://react.dev/), [TypeScript 5](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) | | **Styling & Components** | [Tailwind CSS 4](https://tailwindcss.com/), [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) (New York style), Lucide Icons | | **Database & ORM** | [Prisma 6](https://www.prisma.io/) with SQLite (zero-config local) & PostgreSQL (production ready) | | **API & Backend** | Next.js Edge & Node.js Serverless API Routes (`src/app/api/*`) | | **AI Integration** | Google Gemini API & OpenRouter provider abstraction via `z-ai-web-dev-sdk` | | **Testing Framework** | Native Node.js Test Runner (`node:test`, `node:assert/strict`) — 20/20 passed | | **Containerization** | Multi-stage production [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile) & [Docker Compose](docker/docker-compose.yml) | | **Reverse Proxy** | Caddy Gateway configuration included | --- ## 🏗️ System Architecture ``` [ User Browser ] │ ▼ (HTTP / JSON) ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Next.js 16 Unified Platform │ │ │ │ ┌───────────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Frontend Dashboard │ │ REST API Layer │ │ │ │ 12 Interactive Views │──▶│ /api/connections │ │ │ │ Dark / Light Themes │ │ /api/webhooks │ │ │ │ Realtime Status │ │ /api/testing │ │ │ │ Report Previews │ │ /api/snapshots │ │ │ └───────────────────────┘ │ /api/ai-debugger │ │ │ └───────────┬───────────┘ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────┘ │ ┌────────────────────┴────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ Prisma ORM │ │ GHL API Client │ │ SQLite (Dev) / Postgres (Prod│ │ services.leadconnectorhq │ │ 14 Data Models & Audit Log │ │ (SSRF-Protected / HMAC SHA) │ └───────────────────────────────┘ └───────────────────────────────┘ ▲ │ [ GoHighLevel Platform ] ``` --- ## ⚡ Quick Start ### 1. Clone & Install ```bash git clone https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/ghl-devops-toolkit.git cd ghl-devops-toolkit # Install dependencies npm install --legacy-peer-deps ``` ### 2. Configure Environment ```bash cp .env.example .env ``` *By default, `DEMO_MODE="true"` is enabled, allowing you to test all 8 modules immediately without needing live GoHighLevel API keys.* ### 3. Initialize Database ```bash npm run db:push npm run db:generate ``` ### 4. Launch the Toolkit ```bash npm run dev ``` Open **[http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000)** in your browser. The application will automatically seed with sample connections, webhook captures, workflow simulations, and test suites. --- ## 🐳 Docker Deployment To launch with Docker Compose: ```bash docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build -d ``` The application will be running on port `3000` with persistent SQLite storage mounted in a dedicated volume. --- ## 🧪 Automated Testing & QA The project includes an automated test suite verifying request simulation, signature verification, assertion engine operators, and snapshot validation logic: ```bash # Run unit & integration tests npm test # Run TypeScript type check npm run type-check # Run linter npm run lint # Compile production build npm run build ``` ### Test Verification Matrix ``` ▶ GHL API Client - Demo Mode Request Execution ✔ executes /contacts GET request with simulated response ✔ executes /contacts POST request with 201 Created ✔ executes /opportunities GET request ✔ executes /calendars/events GET request ✔ executes /locations and /users GET requests ✔ provides valid GHL demo endpoints list ✔ GHL API Client - # Gemini Agent Reliability Kit (GAR Kit)

[![ci](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-reliability-kit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-reliability-kit/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%20%7C%203.11%20%7C%203.12-blue)](pyproject.toml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE)

Most Gemini agent failures are not "the model is dumb". They are concrete, boring, and repeatable:

- the model picks the right tool but drops a required argument,
- it returns JSON that is 95% correct and unusable,
- it retries four times with the same backoff and burns your quota,
- one case in the suite takes 9 seconds and nobody notices until it is in production.

GAR Kit turns a handful of labelled cases into a **report card** that names the failure, on the case, in CI,
before your users find it. Zero dependencies, no network or API key needed for the default path.

```
GAR Kit report card  suite=smoke  model=mock-1  cases=6
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ID                  PASS  SCHEMA  TOOLS  ARGS  RETRY  LATENCY  COST($)
tool-basic          no    ok      ok     ok    FAIL   ok       0.000000
schema-json         no    ok      ok     ok    FAIL   ok       0.000000
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
pass rate 0.0%  (gate 90.0%)  -> FAIL
failures by check: retry=6

EVIDENCE
  tool-basic / retry: 5 attempts exceeded budget of 3
  schema-json / retry: 5 attempts exceeded budget of 3
```

## Quickstart

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-reliability-kit
cd gemini-agent-reliability-kit
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/Scripts/activate   # Windows; use .venv/bin/activate on macOS/Linux
pip install -e ".[dev]"

gar run --suite suites/smoke.json --provider mock --report reports/smoke.md
```

Add `--fail-on-gate` to turn the gate into an exit code: `1` when the gate is missed, `0` when it passes. Without
the flag a failing card still exits `0`, which is what you want for an exploratory run and not what you want in CI.
The mock provider is deterministic: same suite in, same card out, no credentials.

## Running against a real model

```bash
# PowerShell
$env:GEMINI_API_KEY = "...."
gar run --suite suites/smoke.json --provider gemini --model gemini-2.0-flash `
        --report reports/gemini-smoke.md --json reports/gemini-smoke.json --fail-on-gate
```

The Gemini provider uses the plain REST endpoint over `urllib` — no SDK, no transitive dependency tree.
It reports what actually happened: `attempts`, `backoff_ms`, `usageMetadata` token counts. Nothing is estimated
except the price table, and if the response carries no usage metadata the cost is reported as `0`, never invented.

## What gets checked

| check | question it answers | failure looks like |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | Does the structured output satisfy the declared subset of JSON Schema? | missing key, wrong type, unparsable JSON |
| `tool_call` | Did the model pick the expected tool (and not a dangerous one)? | `delete_everything` instead of `get_weather` |
| `args` | Did the call carry every required argument with the expected value? | `{}` sent to a tool that needs `city` |
| `retry` | Did the turn stay inside the attempt budget with growing backoff? | 5 attempts, flat 40 ms spacing |
| `latency` | Did the case stay inside `max_latency_ms`? | p95 regression nobody caught in review |

Every failure carries a one-line evidence string naming the case and the check, so a red CI job tells you what to
fix instead of just that something is wrong.

    {
      "id": "tool-basic",
      "prompt": "What is the weather in Lahore right now?",

        "type": "object",
        "properties

[![ci](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-reliability-kit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-reliability-kit/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%20%7C%203.11%20%7C%203.12-blue)](pyproject.toml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE)

Most Gemini agent failures are not "the model is dumb". They are concrete, boring, and repeatable:

- the model picks the right tool but drops a required argument,
- it returns JSON that is 95% correct and unusable,
- it retries four times with the same backoff and burns your quota,
- one case in the suite takes 9 seconds and nobody notices until it is in production.

GAR Kit turns a handful of labelled cases into a **report card** that names the failure, on the case, in CI,
before your users find it. Zero dependencies, no network or API key needed for the default path.

```
GAR Kit report card  suite=smoke  model=mock-1  cases=6
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ID                  PASS  SCHEMA  TOOLS  ARGS  RETRY  LATENCY  COST($)
tool-basic          no    ok      ok     ok    FAIL   ok       0.000000
schema-json         no    ok      ok     ok    FAIL   ok       0.000000
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
pass rate 0.0%  (gate 90.0%)  -> FAIL
failures by check: retry=6

EVIDENCE
  tool-basic / retry: 5 attempts exceeded budget of 3
  schema-json / retry: 5 attempts exceeded budget of 3
```

## Quickstart

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/gemini-agent-reliability-kit
cd gemini-agent-reliability-kit
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/Scripts/activate   # Windows; use .venv/bin/activate on macOS/Linux
pip install -e ".[dev]"

gar run --suite suites/smoke.json --provider mock --report reports/smoke.md
```

Add `--fail-on-gate` to turn the gate into an exit code: `1` when the gate is missed, `0` when it passes. Without
the flag a failing card still exits `0`, which is what you want for an exploratory run and not what you want in CI.
The mock provider is deterministic: same suite in, same card out, no credentials.

## Running against a real model

```bash
# PowerShell
$env:GEMINI_API_KEY = "...."
gar run --suite suites/smoke.json --provider gemini --model gemini-2.0-flash `
        --report reports/gemini-smoke.md --json reports/gemini-smoke.json --fail-on-gate
```

The Gemini provider uses the plain REST endpoint over `urllib` — no SDK, no transitive dependency tree.
It reports what actually happened: `attempts`, `backoff_ms`, `usageMetadata` token counts. Nothing is estimated
except the price table, and if the response carries no usage metadata the cost is reported as `0`, never invented.

## What gets checked

| check | question it answers | failure looks like |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | Does the structured output satisfy the declared subset of JSON Schema? | missing key, wrong type, unparsable JSON |
| `tool_call` | Did the model pick the expected tool (and not a dangerous one)? | `delete_everything` instead of `get_weather` |
| `args` | Did the call carry every required argument with the expected value? | `{}` sent to a tool that needs `city` |
| `retry` | Did the turn stay inside the attempt budget with growing backoff? | 5 attempts, flat 40 ms spacing |
| `latency` | Did the case stay inside `max_latency_ms`? | p95 regression nobody caught in review |

Every failure carries a one-line evidence string naming the case and the check, so a red CI job tells you what to
fix instead of just that something is wrong.

## Suite format

```json
{
  "name": "smoke",
  "gate": {"min_pass_rate": 0.9},
  "cases": [
    {
      "id": "tool-basic",
      "prompt": "What is the weather in Lahore right now?",
      "tools": [{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
        "required": ["city"]}}],
      "expected_tool": "get_weather",
      "expected_args": {"city": "Lahore"},
      "max_latency_ms": 4000,
      "max_attempts": 3
    }
  ]
}
```

Anything you cannot assert on is omitted; a case with no `expected_tool` simply skips the tool checks.

## Example artefacts

Committed under [`docs/`](docs) so the output is visible without running anything:

- `example-report-pass.md` / `.json` — a clean run
- `example-report-fail-retry-storm.md` — retry budget blown, everything else fine
- `example-report-fail-wrong-tool.md` — correct arguments, wrong tool

## Architecture

```
suite.json --> runner --> provider (mock | gemini)
                              |
                              +--> Turn(text, tool_calls, usage, latency_ms, attempts, backoff_ms)
                              |
                 checks: schema | tool_call | args | retry | latency
                              |
                 CaseResult --> aggregates (pass rate, p50/p95, cost) --> report card
                              |
                              +--> markdown / json / text  -->  exit code (CI gate)
```

Design notes, extension points and the reasoning behind the check set live in
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md). A longer write-up on why the output is a named failure rather than a
score: [`docs/article-01-let-your-agent-failures-name-themselves.md`](docs/article-01-let-your-agent-failures-name-themselves.md).

## Not in scope (on purpose)

- No leaderboard of model scores. A model benchmark ages badly; a suite you own does not.
- No LLM-as-judge. Judging with a model makes the harness as flaky as the thing it measures.
- No dashboard. A markdown card diffed in a PR is a better review artefact than a chart nobody opens.

## Status

- [x] Eval suite format + runner
- [x] Four reliability checks with per-case evidence
- [x] Mock provider (offline, deterministic) + live Gemini REST provider
- [x] Report card: text / markdown / JSON, CI gate via exit code
- [x] 53 tests, no network or credentials required
- [x] CI on Python 3.10 / 3.11 / 3.12
- [ ] Vertex AI provider
- [ ] HTML report card

readme.excerpt:
# Restock Radar

A Shopify app that helps merchants recover lost sales from stockouts via back-in-stock alerts and preorders.

## Features

- 🔔 **Back-in-Stock Alerts** — Notify customers when out-of-stock products return to inventory
- 🔄 **Preorders** — Allow customers to pre-order unavailable products
- 📊 **Analytics** — Track subscribers, notifications, click-through rates, and attributed orders
- ✉️ **Custom Email Templates** — Brand your restock notification emails

## Architecture

```
restock-radar/
├── app/
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── NotifyButton.jsx       # Storefront notify button
│   │   └── PolarisProvider.jsx    # Polaris theme provider
│   ├── models/
│   │   ├── dashboard.server.jsx   # Dashboard stats
│   │   ├── subscriber.server.jsx  # Subscriber CRUD
│   │   ├── shop.server.jsx        # Shop settings
│   │   └── restock-event.server.jsx # Restock tracking
│   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── app._index.jsx         # Main dashboard
│   │   ├── app.subscribers.jsx    # Subscriber list + export
│   │   ├── app.settings.jsx       # Settings + email template
│   │   └── api.webhooks.jsx       # Webhook handlers
│   ├── shopify.server.jsx         # OAuth + API config
│   └── root.jsx                    # Remix root
├── prisma/
│   └── schema.prisma               # Database schema
├── extensions/
│   └── restock-notify/            # Shopify app extension
│       └── blocks/
│           └── notify-button/
├── package.json
├── shopify.app.toml
└── remix.config.js
```

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+
- Shopify Partner account
- Development store

### Setup

```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install

# Set up environment variables
cp .env.example .env

# Set your Shopify credentials
SHOPIFY_API_KEY=your_api_key
SHOPIFY_API_SECRET=your_api_secret
SHOPIFY_APP_URL=https://your-app-url.com
DATABASE_URL=file:./dev.db

# Start the dev server
npm run dev
```

### Environment Variables

```env
SHOPIFY_API_KEY=your_api_key
SHOPIFY_API_SECRET=your_api_secret
SHOPIFY_APP_URL=https://your-app-url.com
SHOPIFY_APP_SHOPIFY_EMAIL=admin@example.com
SHOPIFY_APP_BOT_USERNAME=your-bot-username
DATABASE_URL="file:./dev.db"

SENDGRID_API_KEY=your_sendgrid_key
TWILIO_API_KEY=your_twilio_key
```

## Deployment

### Shopify App Deployment

1. `npm run prepare:app`
2. Deploy via Shopify CLI:
   ```bash
   npm run deploy
   ```

### Custom Hosting

The app can be deployed to any Node.js host that supports Remix:

- [Fly.io](https://fly.io)
- [Railway](https://railway.app)
- [Vercel](https://vercel.com)

### Environment Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| SHOPIFY_API_KEY | Your Shopify app API key |
| SHOPIFY_API_SECRET | Your Shopify app API secret |
| SHOPIFY_APP_URL | Your app URL (e.g., https://restock-radar.example.com) |
| DATABASE_URL | Database connection string |
| SENDGRID_API_KEY | Email sending API key |
| TWILIO_API_KEY | SMS sending API key |

## Development

### Running Dev Server

```bash
npm run dev
```

### Testing

```bash
npm run test
```

## App Store Requirements

- Secure authentication and least-privilege access ✓
- Proper tenant isolation ✓
- Input validation and error handling ✓
- Rate-limit handling and webhook verification ✓
- Reliable data storage where required ✓
- Privacy and data deletion workflows ✓
- Automated tests and development-store testing ✓
- Clear installation and troubleshooting documentation ✓
- No exposed API keys or credentials ✓

## License

MIT

# NexGen Financial Experts — Website

Production rebuild of https://nexgenfinancialexperts.com after an SEO-spam compromise of the original WordPress site. Next.js 16 (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS 4 + shadcn/ui + Prisma (SQLite).

**Business:** NexGen Financial Experts — accounting, tax, audit & business advisory, Fort Lauderdale, FL.
**Contact:** +1 (954) 306-3823 · WhatsApp +1 (954) 770-1568 · paudalus@nexgenfinancialexperts.com · 1975 East Sunrise Blvd, Suite 705, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33304

---

## Pages

| Route | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/` | Home: hero, 6 service pillars, industries, why-us, featured services, about teaser, testimonials, FAQs, CTA |
| `/about` | Firm story, mission, values |
| `/services` | Services hub (12 cards) |
| `/services/[slug]` | 12 service landing pages (all original WP slugs preserved) |
| `/insights` + `/insights/[slug]` | Blog hub + 3 educational articles |
| `/contact` | Working form + NAP + map |
| `/privacy-policy`, `/terms-of-use` | Legal drafts (flagged for review) |
| 404 | Custom recovery page |
| `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt` | Auto-generated; 301s from legacy URLs (`/aboutus`, `/blog`, `/home`) |
| `POST /api/contact` | Validated contact endpoint (rate limit + honeypot + time trap; stores to DB; optional SMTP email) |

## Quick Start

```bash
bun install          # or npm install
cp .env.example .env # adjust if needed (SMTP optional)
bun run db:push      # create SQLite schema
bun run dev          # http://localhost:3000
```

Production:

```bash
bun run build && bun run start
```

## Environment

See `.env.example`. Only `DATABASE_URL` is required; SMTP variables enable contact-form email delivery. Never commit real secrets.

## Key Files

```
src/lib/site.ts        — NAP config, nav, redirects (single source of truth)
src/lib/services.ts    — all 12 service definitions + SEO metadata
src/lib/articles.ts    — educational articles
src/components/site/   — header, footer, forms, shared blocks
src/app/api/contact/   — secure contact endpoint
prisma/schema.prisma   — ContactSubmission model
public/images/         — official logo, favicon set, hero image
```

## Design System

- Brand colors sampled from the official logo: magenta `#C01040`, blue `#4090D0`, navy `#0B1F3A`, white.
- Fonts: Inter (body), Source Serif 4 (display headings) via `next/font`.
- Logo: `public/images/nexgen-logo.png` (recovered from the official domain). Favicon derived from the logo mark at `src/app/icon.png`.

## Security Notes

- Original WordPress site was compromised (hidden casino-link widgets + spam posts — see `download/docs/security-audit.md`). This rebuild contains no WordPress code path.
- Contact form: server-side validation, per-IP rate limiting (5/10 min), honeypot + time-trap, no PII in URLs, data stored only in the DB (email optional via SMTP).
- Security headers configured in `next.config.ts` (CSP, frame-options, nosniff, referrer/permissions policy).

## Documentation

Full project deliverables (audit, security, competitor research, keyword map, content & marketing strategy, QA, deployment, recovery checklist, analytics, 90-day roadmap) live in **`download/docs/`**.

repositories.name: envscope
repositories.description: CLI that audits .env files against .env.example and a JSON schema without ever printing secrets. DevSecOps, Python.

readme.excerpt:
envscope: zero-dependency CLI that audits .env files against .env.example and a JSON schema, never printing secret values.

## Features
- Drift detection (missing, extra, empty, duplicate keys)
- Type validation: string, int, float, bool, port, url, email, pattern, choices
- Duplicate detection
- Secret-aware (values flagged secret are never printed)
- CI-friendly (--json, --sarif, stable exit codes)
- SARIF 2.1.0 export for GitHub code scanning
- Zero dependencies (Python 3.9+)
- Fast (parses thousands of keys in milliseconds)

## Requirements
- Python 3.11 or newer
- macOS, Linux, or Windows

## Install
```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/envscope.git
cd envscope
python -m pip install -e .
```

## Usage
```bash
envscope check [--env .env --example .env.example --schema envscope.json --strict --json --sarif PATH --quiet --no-color]
envscope init --example .env.example --out envscope.json
envscope version
```

## Schema format
envscope.json: `{"variables": {"APP_ENV":{"type":"string","choices":["development","staging","production"]},...}}`
Flat `{"PORT":"port"}` also accepted.

## CI example
```yaml
- name: Validate environment contract
  run: |
    python -m pip install -e .
    envscope check --strict --json > envscope-report.json
  env:
    PYTHONPATH: src
```

## SARIF / code scanning
`envscope check --sarif envscope.sarif` writes a SARIF 2.1.0 log next to the normal
output. Findings map to one rule per issue code (`parse`, `duplicate`, `missing`,
`empty`, `invalid`, `extra`) with error/warning levels, so GitHub code scanning can
group and annotate them inline on the offending dotenv line.

The log only contains key names, line numbers and envscope's own messages. Secret
values are never written to it, which is what makes it safe to upload as a build
artifact.

```yaml
- name: Validate environment contract
  run: |
    python -m pip install -e .
    envscope check --strict --sarif envscope.sarif
  env:
    PYTHONPATH: src
  continue-on-error: true

- name: Upload SARIF
  uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  with:
    sarif_file: envscope.sarif
    category: envscope
```

## Tests
42 tests, no dependencies. CI runs on Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13.

## License
MIT

- **Store analytics** (`analytics_*`) — sales totals, order counts, AOV, best sellers, sales trends, discounts, refunds, inventory exposure, product comparisons. Deterministic formulas documented.
- **Product feed quality** (`feed_quality_audit`, `feed_export`) — validates data against marketing-readiness criteria and exports structured feeds.
- **Inventory intelligence** (`inventory_intelligence`) — configurable low-stock thresholds, stale-product detection, reorder suggestions, variant inconsistencies.
- **Marketing preparation** (`marketing_*`) — ad copy drafts, campaign briefs, campaign naming, product grouping by category/priority.

### Safety first

- **Read-only by default**: every tool declares a risk tier (`READ` / `WRITE` / `DESTRUCTIVE`).
- **Plan-and-apply workflow**: bulk writes produce a preview (IDs, current values, proposed values, affected counts, warnings); an approval token is bound to the exact plan hash — changed parameters require a new approval.
- **Audit logging**: every operation is recorded with redacted secrets.
- **Least-privilege guidance**: setup docs show the minimal Admin API scopes.
- **No silent writes, no fabricated results, no fake "approved by Google/Meta" claims.**

---

│  MCP clients: Claude Desktop · Claude Code · Cursor · VS Code · Codex │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                                           │ Model Context Protocol (stdio)
┌──────────────────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────┐
│                       shopify-growth-mcp (this repo)                 │
│  ┌───────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌───────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ Tool registry │  │ Policy engine│  │ Audit log / approvals     │  │
│  │ 61 tools      │  │ READ/WRITE/  │  │ previews, bound tokens,   │  │
│  │ risk-tiered   │  │ DESTRUCTIVE  │  │ redaction                 │  │
│  └──────┬────────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └───────────────────────────┘  │
│         │                  │                                         │
│  ┌──────▼──────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ Shopify GraphQL client: pagination · retries · rate limits ·   │  │
│  │ timeouts · cost awareness · API version pinning (2025-10)      │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Shopify Admin GraphQL API
                        ┌─────────▼─────────┐

                        └───────────────────┘

See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for the full design, data-flow and decision log.

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- Node.js **22.12+** (tested on Node 24).
- No Shopify account required for demo mode.

### 30-second demo (no credentials)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamid-digitalmarketer/shopify-growth-mcp.git
cd shopify-growth-mcp
npm install
npm run build
npx shopify-growth-mcp --demo
```

The server starts in **demo mode** against clearly-labeled fictional store data. Point any MCP client at it (see [docs/client-configuration.md](docs/client-configuration.md)) and ask:

Demo data is synthetic and always labeled `demo: true` — it is **never** silently substituted for a real connection.

### Connect a real Shopify store

1. Create a custom app in Shopify Admin → **Settings → Apps and sales channels → Develop apps**.
2. Grant the **minimum scopes** you need (e.g. `read_products`, `write_products`, `read_orders`, `read_customers`, `read_inventory`).
3. Install the app and copy the Admin API access token.
4. Configure:

# PinVault — Pinterest Image & Video Downloader

PinVault is a local-first Chrome extension (Manifest V3) for saving Pinterest images and **directly accessible** videos with the best available resolution, smart filenames, bulk download queues, duplicate detection, collections, and CSV/JSON inventory export.

**No build step, no runtime dependencies, vanilla JavaScript.** Request only the permissions it needs and never transmits your data.

> **Legal reminder:** Save only content you are authorized to save. Respect creator rights and applicable copyright law. PinVault does not bypass DRM, logins, CAPTCHAs, or rate limits.

## Features

- **Hover quick download** — a download button appears over Pinterest pins (home feed, boards, search, pin pages).
- **Popup quick download** — paste a pin URL (including `pin.it` short links) and download it directly.
- **Page scan** — collect media from the current board/search/pin page into the dashboard.
- **Bulk downloads** — bounded-concurrency queue (default 3), progress, pause, resume, cancel, and retry with backoff.
- **Filters & selection** — orientation, minimum dimensions, format, duplicate status; select all / deselect / individual selection with preview.
- **Highest accessible resolution** — picks the widest accessible CDN variant and excludes login-walled variants.
- **Smart naming** — configurable templates: `pinterest-title-001.jpg`, `board-name_pin-id.jpg`, `yyyy-mm-dd_pin-id.webp`; sanitized, path-traversal-safe filenames.
- **Duplicate prevention** — normalized media URLs and pin ids keep repeats out of your Downloads.
- **Collections** — save collected media records into named local collections.
- **History** — review past downloads, retry failures, clear independently of Chrome's download history.
- **CSV/JSON export** — media inventory with pin URL, dimensions, format, and status.
- **Light/dark/system theme**, keyboard-navigable, accessible UI.
- **Video support** — direct MP4/WebM downloads; segmented HLS and DRM-protected videos are explicitly marked unsupported (never bypassed).
- **Privacy** — local-first; one-click "Erase all PinVault data".

## Install (developer mode, load unpacked)

1. Download the release ZIP (`dist/pinvault-pinterest-downloader-1.0.0.zip`) and extract it, **or** clone the repository.
2. Open `chrome://extensions`.
3. Enable **Developer mode** (top-right).
4. Click **Load unpacked** and select the folder that contains `manifest.json` (the project root, e.g. `D:\pin extension\PinVault`).
5. Pin the PinVault toolbar icon. Visit a Pinterest board and hover a pin to test.

To repackage from source: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build.ps1`.

## Usage

### Quick download
- **Hover:** hover any pin → click the download button.
- **Popup:** click the PinVault toolbar icon → paste a pin URL → **Download**. The popup also shows the current page's media count, a mini queue, and recent history.

### Bulk download
1. Open the dashboard (`chrome://extensions` → PinVault → Details → Extension options, or right-click the toolbar icon → Options).
2. Go to **Collect** → **Scan current page** (or scroll and re-scan to capture lazy-loaded pins).
3. Filter and select media, then **Download selected**.
4. Watch progress in **Bulk downloads**; pause, cancel, retry as needed.

### Collections, history, exports
- **Collections:** create a named collection and add selected media records.
- **History:** review downloads, retry failed items, clear history.
- **Export:** export the current inventory as CSV or JSON.

4. Click **Load unpacked** and select the folder that contains `manifest.json` (the project root, e.g. `D:\pin extension\PinVault`).
5. Pin the PinVault toolbar icon. Visit a Pinterest board and hover a pin to test.

To repackage from source: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build.ps1`.

## Usage

### Quick download
- **Hover:** hover any pin → click the download button.
- **Popup:** click the PinVault toolbar icon → paste a pin URL → **Download**. The popup also shows the current page's media count, a mini queue, and recent history.

### Bulk download
1. Open the dashboard (`chrome://extensions` → PinVault → Details → Extension options, or right-click the toolbar icon → Options).
2. Go to **Collect** → **Scan current page** (or scroll and re-scan to capture lazy-loaded pins).
3. Filter and select media, then **Download selected**.
4. Watch progress in **Bulk downloads**; pause, cancel, retry as needed.

### Collections, history, exports
- **Collections:** create a named collection and add selected media records.
- **History:** review downloads, retry failed items, clear history.
- **Export:** export the current inventory as CSV or JSON.

## Permissions explained

| Permission | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `storage` | Store settings/history/queue/collections/duplicate index locally |
| `downloads` | Save media through Chrome's Downloads API |
| `activeTab` | Read the active Pinterest tab when you click the popup |
| Host: `*://*.pinterest.com/*`, `*://*.pinimg.com/*`, `https://pin.it/*` | Operate only on Pinterest and its media CDN |

## Privacy & copyright notice

PinVault is local-first: no accounts, no tracking, no analytics, no uploads. All data stays in `chrome.storage.local` and can be erased at any time. See [docs/privacy-policy.md](docs/privacy-policy.md). You are responsible for having a lawful basis to save, reproduce, or redistribute content.

## Developer setup

Requirements: Node.js ≥ 16 (for tests/build validation), PowerShell 5.1+ (Windows) or any shell for `node`.

```bash
# Run the automated test suite
node tests/run-tests.js

# Validate + package (Windows)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build.ps1
```

Project layout:

```
background/   service worker (queue, downloads, persistence, recovery)
content/      Pinterest page integration (overlay, scan, MutationObserver)
popup/        toolbar popup UI
dashboard/    full-page manager UI
lib/          shared, dependency-free, unit-testable modules
icons/        original icon assets (PNG + SVG)
tests/        Node unit tests + fixtures
scripts/      build + validation scripts
docs/         architecture, privacy, troubleshooting, limitations, listing
```

## Tests

`tests/run-tests.js` is a zero-dependency runner. It covers filename sanitization, URL validation, pin-extractor parsing, duplicate detection, queue logic, and CSV/JSON export correctness.

```bash
node tests/run-tests.js
# => TOTAL: 65 passed, 0 failed
```

## Known limitations

- Videos: only directly accessible MP4/WebM are downloadable; segmented HLS (`m3u8`) and DRM-protected videos are reported as unsupported.
- Private/login-gated content requires your own authorized, signed-in session; PinVault never bypasses authentication.
- Pinterest may change its DOM; automatic detection is defensive but not immune. Manual URL paste always works as a fallback.
- PinVault saves the highest **accessible** variant; it cannot recover originals Pinterest does not expose.
- No format conversion in 1.0.0.

Full details: [docs/limitations.md](docs/limitations.md) and [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md).

## Roadmap

- Perceptual near-duplicate detection (visual similarity) as an optional, fully-local mode
- Optional import/export of settings
- Internationalization (i18n) framework and first additional languages
- Format conversion behind a safe, policy-reviewed implementation
- Verified screenshots and Chrome Web Store submission (after final branding and support contact)

## Contributing

See [.github/CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) if present, otherwise: open an issue first for significant changes, keep changes dependency-free, add tests for lib changes, run `node tests/run-tests.js` and the build script before submitting a PR. Never commit credentials, user data, downloaded private content, or secrets.

Search engines decide independently how and when to display rich snippets or cite pages in AI Overviews. Dynamic Schema Generator never promises guaranteed rankings or rich snippet placements. --- ## ⚡ Core Features ``` +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Dynamic Schema Generator Engine | +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | | v v [ Standard WordPress Content ] [ Elementor Layouts ] • Posts & Pages • Post Document Tree Traversal • Hierarchical Categories • Accordion Widgets -> FAQPage • Post Authors -> Person • Toggle Widgets -> FAQPage • Featured Images -> ImageObject • Heading Widgets -> Section Outline | | +---------------------+---------------------+ | v +---------------------------+ | Schema.org Graph Builder | +---------------------------+ • Organization / LocalBusiness (#organization) • WebSite (#website) + SearchAction • WebPage (#webpage) + BreadcrumbList (#breadcrumb) • Article / BlogPosting (#article) • Service (#service) + Offers & Pricing • FAQPage (#faq) | v +---------------------------+ | In-House Validator | | Syntax, @ids, Types | +---------------------------+ | v +---------------------------+ | Clean JSON-LD Output | | Injected into | +---------------------------+ ``` ### 1. Interconnected Schema `@graph` Architecture Generates a consolidated `@graph` array linking entities via persistent `#` URIs: - **`Organization` / `LocalBusiness`:** Brand identity, legal name, telephone, email, physical address (`PostalAddress`), geographic coordinates (`GeoCoordinates`), opening hours (`OpeningHoursSpecification`), and authoritative social profiles (`sameAs`). - **`WebSite`:** Site entity with `SearchAction` potentialAction for Google sitelinks search box. - **`WebPage`:** Page entity linked to site hierarchy, authors, and canonical URLs. - **`BreadcrumbList`:** Hierarchical navigation trail with numerical `ListItem` positions. - **`Article` / `BlogPosting`:** Headline, datePublished, dateModified, author (`Person`), and featured image (`ImageObject`). - **`Service`:** Mapped landing page service offerings, category, provider link, and explicit pricing (`Offer`). - **`FAQPage`:** Question and answer pairs extracted from manual post configuration or Elementor widgets. ### 2. Dedicated Elementor Integration Layer - **Non-Invasive Tree Traversal:** Directly reads `_elementor_data` document structures without DOM rendering penalties. - **Automatic FAQ Extraction:** Converts `accordion` and `toggle` widgets into Schema.org `FAQPage` markup. - **Heading Outline Inspection:** Extracts `heading` widgets for section context. - **Zero-Dependency Fallback:** If Elementor is inactive or missing, the plugin operates smoothly on standard WordPress content without throwing errors. ### 3. Business Information & Local SEO Manager Full management interface under **Dynamic Schema > Business Info**: - 12 supported business types: `Organization`, `LocalBusiness`, `ProfessionalService`, `LegalService`, `MedicalBusiness`, `FinancialService`, `Store`, etc. - Precision geographic latitude and longitude for Google Maps and Local 3-Pack proximity. - Sanitized `sameAs` array for knowledge graph establishment across LinkedIn, X, GitHub, and corporate directories. ### 4. Service Schema Builder & Page Mapping - Map specific services to dedicated landing pages. - Optional, honest pricing: prices are only emitted when explicitly supplied by the administrator. Never fabricates estimates or pricing ranges. ### 5. In-House Schema Preview & Validator - Select any published post or the global homepage to inspect the live generated JSON-LD. - Real-time linting detects missing required properties, invalid `@context`, duplicate `@id`s, or malformed JSON syntax. - One-click copy and direct links to the **Google Rich Results Test** and **Schema.org Validator**. ### 6. Conflict Safeguards & Diagnostics - Detects existing active installations of **Yoast SEO**, **Rank Math**, **All in One SEO (AIOSEO)**, and **SEOPress**. - Provides duplicate-output suppression and post-level exclusion checkboxes. --- ## 🗂️ Technical Directory Structure ``` dynamic-schema-generator/ ├── dynamic-schema-generator.php # Main bootstrap & autoloader ├── uninstall.php # Safe uninstaller with clean option ├── readme.txt # WordPress.org plugin directory specification ├── README.md # Comprehensive GitHub repository guide ├── LICENSE # MIT License ├── composer.json # PSR-4 autoloading & developer scripts ├── phpunit.xml.dist # PHPUnit test configuration ├── docker-compose.yml # Local WordPress 6.6 + MySQL 8.0 demo ├── .gitignore # Clean Git exclusion rules ├── .github/ │ └── workflows/ │ └── ci.yml # CI Matrix across PHP 7.4 - 8.3 ├── includes/ │ ├── class-plugin.php # Lifecycle orchestrator │ ├── class-activator.php # Activation & default options │ ├── class-deactivator.php # Deactivation & transient cleanup │ ├── class-settings.php # Settings getter/setter & sanitization │ ├── class-admin.php # Admin screens, menus, AJAX & meta boxes │ ├── class-business-manager.php # Organization & LocalBusiness profile │ ├── class-service-manager.php # Service definitions & page mapping │ ├── class-faq-manager.php # FAQ management & deduplication │ ├── class-schema-generator.php # Core @graph entity generator │ ├── class-schema-validator.php # Syntax & Schema.org property linter │ ├── class-schema-output.php # wp_head output renderer │ ├── class-diagnostics.php # Health checks, telemetry & audit logs │ └── integrations/ │ ├── interface-page-builder-adapter.php # Modular adapter interface │ └── class-elementor-adapter.php # Elementor JSON data parser ├── admin/ │ ├── css/admin-style.css # Responsive WordPress admin styling │ ├── js/admin-script.js # AJAX preview, copy tool, log cleaner │ └── views/ # 9 modular admin view templates ├── languages/ │ └── dynamic-schema-generator.pot # Internationalization template └── tests/ ├── bootstrap.php # WordPress mocking harness ├── run-tests.php # Standalone test runner ├── test-settings.php ├── test-business-manager.php ├── test-service-manager.php ├── test-faq-manager.php ├── test-elementor-adapter.php ├── test-schema-generator.php └── test-schema-validation.php ``` --- ## 🚀 Installation & Quick Start ### Method 1: WordPress Admin Upload (ZIP Archive) 1. Download `dynamic-schema-generator.zip` from the [Releases](https://github.com/hamid-digitalmarketer/dynamic-schema-generator/releases) tab. 2. [![CI](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/firebase-ai-starter-kit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hamids-ai-automations/firebase-ai-starter-kit/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
