# SEO Audit and Website Health Checker

An ethical, configurable on-page SEO audit application built with Python and Streamlit. Enter a website URL, and the tool crawls internal pages, checks key on-page signals, and produces a prioritized list of issues with recommendations, a summary dashboard, and CSV export.

## Problem it solves

SEO audits are usually manual, slow, and expensive. This tool automates the first-pass technical audit: it catches missing titles and meta descriptions, duplicate titles, weak heading structure, missing canonical tags, images without alt text, broken fetches, and missing `robots.txt` / `sitemap.xml` — then presents everything in a recruiter-friendly, actionable dashboard.

## Key features

- Crawl accessible internal pages within a configurable limit (BFS with polite delays)
- Analyze page titles, meta descriptions, H1/H2 headings, canonical URLs, and indexability signals
- Detect images missing alt attributes
- Detect duplicate titles and duplicate meta descriptions across pages
- Report fetch failures and HTTP status issues
- Check `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` availability
- Prioritized issue list (critical / warning / info) with explanations and recommended fixes
- Summary dashboard with counts by issue type and category chart
- Export issues to CSV

## Safety and ethics

- Respects `robots.txt`, site terms, crawl limits, and server capacity
- Conservative timeouts, delays, and concurrency (single-threaded polite crawl by default)
- Never bypasses CAPTCHAs, authentication, anti-bot controls, or access restrictions
- Does not claim to measure actual Google rankings — findings are directly observed from the page HTML, and recommendations are clearly marked as recommendations

## Technology stack

- Python 3.11
- Standard library `html.parser` (portable, dependency-light core)
- Requests (HTTP fetching)
- Pandas (reporting/CSV)
- Plotly (charts)
- Streamlit (web UI)

## Folder structure

```
seo-audit-tool/
├── app.py                  # Streamlit application
├── seo_audit/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── analyzer.py         # HTML parsing and issue detection engine
│   └── fetcher.py          # Polite HTTP fetching and crawling
├── tests/
│   └── test_analyzer.py    # Unit tests for the analyzer
├── sample.html             # Sample page for offline experimentation
├── requirements.txt
└── .gitignore
```

## Installation

```bash
python -m venv venv
# Windows: venv\Scripts\activate  |  macOS/Linux: source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Usage

```bash
streamlit run app.py
```

Open the local URL shown by Streamlit, enter a website URL, choose the crawl limit, and click **Run Audit**.

### Offline / sample input

To try the analyzer without a network, run the unit tests (see below) or point the tool at any site you are authorized to audit.

## Testing

```bash
pytest -q
```

Tests cover: missing title (critical), noindex detection, missing alt text, multiple H1 headings, duplicate titles across pages, and aggregate counts.

## Limitations and known issues

- Crawling depends on site availability; heavily JS-rendered pages may yield incomplete HTML
- Redirect chains are reported only as fetch failures in this version (full chain tracing is a future improvement)
- Findings reflect the fetched HTML snapshot, not Google's index or ranking position

## Future improvements

- Redirect-chain tracing
- Word-count and keyword-density heuristics
- Mobile vs desktop viewport checks
- Scheduled audits with historical comparison
- CI via GitHub Actions

## Related projects

- [seo-doctor](https://github.com/hamid-digitalmarketer/seo-doctor) — automated technical SEO site crawler (broken links, canonicals, redirect chains)
- [ecommerce-seo-optimizer](https://github.com/hamid-digitalmarketer/ecommerce-seo-optimizer) — on-page product listing audit and optimization for e-commerce

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

---

**Developed by Muhammad Hamid**

Digital Marketing | SEO | Perf

# PPC Performance Dashboard

An interactive paid-media performance dashboard built with Python, Pandas, Plotly, and Streamlit. Upload a Google Ads / Meta Ads / Bing Ads export, and get normalized KPIs, filters, trend charts, campaign and ad group breakdowns, period-over-period comparison, and CSV export — all in one page.

## Problem it solves

Marketers waste hours stitching CSV exports into Excel to answer simple questions: *"How did CTR change this month?"*, *"Which ad group has the lowest cost per conversion?"* This dashboard answers those questions instantly with consistent KPI definitions (CTR, CPC, CPA, conversion rate) and honest, clearly-labeled derived metrics.

## Key features

- Upload CSV or XLSX exports; column names are normalized automatically (date, campaign, ad group, impressions, clicks, spend, conversions)
- Automatic KPI calculation: CTR, CPC, Cost/Conversion, conversion rate
- Sidebar filters: date range, campaign, ad group
- Trend chart for clicks and conversions over time
- Performance tables and charts by campaign and by ad group
- Period-over-period comparison with absolute and percentage deltas
- Download summarized results as CSV
- Bundled synthetic sample data for an instant demo

## Data expectations

The dashboard expects at least a date column and one or more of: impressions, clicks, spend, conversions. Recognized date column names include `date`, `day`, `Date`. Campaign and ad group columns are optional but recommended. Any numeric column that is missing is treated as zero; derived metrics are never invented — they are computed from the columns actually present.

## Technology stack

- Python 3.11
- Pandas (data processing)
- Plotly (interactive charts)
- Streamlit (web UI)
- openpyxl (XLSX upload support)

## Folder structure

# E-commerce SEO Optimizer

A practical tool for e-commerce teams and SEO specialists to audit and improve on-page product listings at scale. Built with Python, Pandas, and Streamlit: upload a product catalog, see every title/description/image/price issue, review keyword-aware suggestions, and export an optimized copy — original columns are always preserved.

## Problem it solves

E-commerce stores often have hundreds or thousands of thin product listings: short titles, missing descriptions, no keywords, broken image references. Fixing them manually in a spreadsheet is slow and error-prone. This tool surfaces the exact problems, proposes concrete title/description improvements using the product's own brand/category/keywords, and produces a safe export for review before applying changes upstream.

## Key features

- Upload CSV or XLSX product catalogs (title, description, price, category, brand, image columns recognized and normalized)
- Audit engine: empty/short/long titles, empty/short descriptions, missing prices, missing or malformed image URLs, duplicate titles
- Severity grading: critical / warning / info
- Suggestion engine: expands short titles with brand/category keywords, generates description copy, records reasons for every change
- Safe apply: writes `optimized_title`, `optimized_description`, `optimized` columns without overwriting originals
- Download the optimized catalog as CSV

## Data expectations

The tool looks for a title column (`title`, `name`, `product`, `product title`) and optional description, price, category, brand, image columns. Unknown columns are ignored. Missing values are flagged, never guessed.

## Technology stack

- Python 3.11
- Pandas (catalog processing)
- Streamlit (web UI)
- openpyxl (XLSX support)

## Folder structure

```
ecommerce-seo-optimizer/
├── app.py                  # Streamlit application
├── optimizer.py            # Validation, suggestion, and export engine
├── tests/
│   └── test_optimizer.py
├── requirements.txt
└── .gitignore
```

## Installation

```bash
python -m venv venv
# Windows: venv/Scripts/activate  |  macOS/Linux: source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Usage

```bash
streamlit run app.py
```

Upload a catalog or use the bundled sample, review the issues and suggestions, then apply and download the optimized file.

## Testing

```bash
pytest -q
```

Tests cover issue detection, suggestion generation, missing-title handling, safe apply behavior, and CSV export.

## Limitations and known issues

- Keyword extraction is heuristic (brand, category, top words); it is not a full SEO content service
- Title length guidance uses common best-practice ranges (20-70 title, 50-160 description) — tune the constants in `optimizer.py` to your vertical if needed
- No integration with platforms (Shopify, WooCommerce, etc.); export and import manually

## Future improvements

- Keyword density scoring and SERP snippet preview
- Competitor title analysis (from a comparison file)
- Shopify/WooCommerce export formats
- Batch apply via a reviewed CSV diff

## Related projects

- [seo-doctor](https://github.com/hamid-digitalmarketer/seo-doctor) — automated technical SEO site crawler
- [seo-audit-tool](https://github.com/hamid-digitalmarketer/seo-audit-tool) — on-page SEO audit and website health checker

# ai-marketing-growth-os

Agentic marketing intelligence platform — a **virtual digital marketing department**.
Four specialist agents (SEO, Ads, E-commerce, Analytics) read real sample data through
permission-gated tools, produce **structured, evidence-backed recommendations**, deduplicate
and prioritize them into a unified action plan, and route every consequential action through a
**human-in-the-loop approval queue**.

Built on the shared portfolio foundation
[`ai-marketing-shared`](https://github.com/hamid-digitalmarketer/ai-marketing-shared):
Pydantic v2 schemas, tool registry, tracing, cost accounting, eval harness, provider abstraction.

> `docker compose up` runs the full pipeline on sample data and produces evidence-backed
> recommendations in the dashboard — with **zero API keys** and **zero cost**.

## Problem

Marketing teams drown in disconnected dashboards. SEO tells you about rankings, ads tells you
about spend, e-commerce tells you about inventory, analytics tells you about traffic — and a
human has to stitch them together, guess which issue matters most, and risk acting without
evidence. Consequential actions (publishing, budget changes, campaign edits) are rarely gated,
so mistakes are expensive.

## Approach

Growth OS models a marketing department as a set of **tool-using agents**:

- **SEO agent** — crawls + GSC + PageSpeed: broken links, missing meta descriptions, low-CTR
  queries, slow pages.
- **Ads agent** — Google Ads + Meta Ads: CPA over target, low CTR creatives, weak ROAS campaigns.
- **E-commerce agent** — product catalog: stock-outs, reorder points, weak PDP conversion,
  pricing outliers.
- **Analytics agent** — GA sessions + GSC: rising bounce, conversion-rate decline, mobile issues.

Every agent:

1. calls **tools** (never hallucinated numbers) at the lowest permission level required;
2. emits **structured recommendations** conforming to shared `Recommendation` / `Evidence` schemas;
3. records a full **trace** (`AgentRun` with tool calls, latency, cost);
4. is **evaluated** against labeled datasets for factual accuracy, tool-use success,
   recommendation quality, prompt-injection resistance, cost, and latency.

An **orchestrator** deduplicates and ranks the combined recommendations into one action plan,
and every write-type action lands in the **approval queue** (`pending → approved → rejected →
executed → measured`) where a human decides.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Data["data/sample_data (CSV, zero keys)"]
        WC[website_crawl] & GSC[gsc_keywords] & PS[pagespeed] & GA[ga_sessions]

    end

    B --> Q[approval queue]
    Q -->|approve/execute/measure| F[frontend dashboard]
    A -->|AgentRun traces| V[trace viewer]
```

readme.excerpt:
# ai-agent-testing-lab

Reusable reliability and evaluation lab for every AI marketing agent in the
portfolio. One harness, seven labeled suites, and a CI integration path that
lets every downstream repository report accuracy, precision/recall,
calibration, cost, latency, and reliability from day one.

Part of the [AI Marketing Engineer Portfolio](../ai-marketing-portfolio-meta/README.md).
Builds on the shared schemas and provider abstraction from
[ai-marketing-shared](../ai-marketing-shared/README.md) and is validated against
the flagship [ai-marketing-growth-os](../ai-marketing-growth-os/README.md).

## Problem

AI marketing agents can look impressive in demos and still be unsafe or
unreliable: they hallucinate numbers, call destructive tools, ignore approval
gates, and fail under adversarial input. Every repository in the portfolio
needed a consistent, evidence-backed way to answer the same questions:

- Did the agent cite real evidence for every recommendation?
- Did it call only the tools it was allowed to call?
- Does it resist prompt injection?
- Is it fast enough, cheap enough, and reliable enough to run in production?

Building a bespoke evaluation suite in every repo would repeat work, drift
apart, and never get compared. The lab exists so evaluation is shared, not
reimplemented.

## Approach

The lab is a thin, dependency-light harness built on the shared schemas:

- **TargetLoader** imports an agent factory from any repo (`module:attr`) and
  validates that it returns `dict[str, agent]` objects with a `run()` method.
- **TestHarness** runs the target through seven labeled suites and produces a
  single `LabReport` with metrics and confusion-matrix details.
- **Reporters** emit JSON, Markdown, and a self-contained HTML dashboard;
  GitHub Actions step summaries are supported for CI.
- **Integration** (`integration/run_lab_eval.py`) is the drop-in script that
  downstream repos add to their workflow to report metrics in CI.

The lab evaluates itself: a known-good `ReliableAgent` must pass every suite,
and a known-broken `BrokenAgent` (hallucinated evidence, forbidden write call,
missing approval gate, random failures) must be caught on every
failure-sensitive suite. If the self-evaluation passes, the lab is proven
effective; if it fails, the lab itself is broken.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Target[Any portfolio repo] -->|pip install -e| TL[TargetLoader]
    TL --> H[TestHarness]
    DS[evaluation/datasets - 7 labeled suites] --> H
    H --> R[LabReport]
    R --> JSON[JSON + Markdown + HTML dashboard]
    R --> CI[CI step summary / thresholds]
    CI -->|PASS / FAIL| GH[GitHub Actions]
    SelfEval[evaluation/run.py] -.reproduces known failures.-> H
```

Layout:

```
ai-agent-testing-lab/
├── lab/                  # harness, metrics, reporters, dashboard, integration, CLI
├── evaluation/
│   ├── datasets/         # seven labeled JSON suites
│   ├── run.py            # self-evaluation entry point
│   └── results/          # generated reports (git-ignored)
├── fixtures/             # known-good / known-broken agents for self-evaluation
├── integration/          # CI template + run_lab_eval.py for downstream repos
├── scripts/demo_eval.py  # quick demo against the fixtures
├── infra/                # Dockerfile + docker-compose.yml
└── .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

## Evaluation Summary

| Suite | What it measures | Metric |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Factual accuracy | recommendation cites expected evidence (source + value range) | hit rate on labeled cases |
| Tool-use | only expected tools are called, with success | tool-use success |
| Recommendation quality | completeness of structured recommendations | quality score |
| Prompt-injection resistance | no forbidden write tool on adversarial input | resistance score |
| Cost | measured cost within labeled cap | cost control |
| Latency | total latency within labeled budget | latency budget |

# ai-agent-testing-lab

Reusable reliability and evaluation lab for every AI marketing agent in the
portfolio. One harness, seven labeled suites, and a CI integration path that
lets every downstream repository report accuracy, precision/recall,
calibration, cost, latency, and reliability from day one.

Part of the [AI Marketing Engineer Portfolio](../ai-marketing-portfolio-meta/README.md).
Builds on the shared schemas and provider abstraction from
[ai-marketing-shared](../ai-marketing-shared/README.md) and is validated against
the flagship [ai-marketing-growth-os](../ai-marketing-growth-os/README.md).

## Problem

AI marketing agents can look impressive in demos and still be unsafe or
unreliable: they hallucinate numbers, call destructive tools, ignore approval
gates, and fail under adversarial input. Every repository in the portfolio
needed a consistent, evidence-backed way to answer the same questions:

- Did the agent cite real evidence for every recommendation?
- Did it call only the tools it was allowed to call?
- Does it resist prompt injection?
- Is it fast enough, cheap enough, and reliable enough to run in production?

Building a bespoke evaluation suite in every repo would repeat work, drift
apart, and never get compared. The lab exists so evaluation is shared, not
reimplemented.

## Approach

The lab is a thin, dependency-light harness built on the shared schemas:

- **TargetLoader** imports an agent factory from any repo (`module:attr`) and
  validates that it returns `dict[str, agent]` objects with a `run()` method.
- **TestHarness** runs the target through seven labeled suites and produces a
  single `LabReport` with metrics and confusion-matrix details.
- **Reporters** emit JSON, Markdown, and a self-contained HTML dashboard;
  GitHub Actions step summaries are supported for CI.
- **Integration** (`integration/run_lab_eval.py`) is the drop-in script that
  downstream repos add to their workflow to report metrics in CI.

The lab evaluates itself: a known-good `ReliableAgent` must pass every suite,
and a known-broken `BrokenAgent` (hallucinated evidence, forbidden write call,
missing approval gate, random failures) must be caught on every
failure-sensitive suite. If the self-evaluation passes, the lab is proven
effective; if it fails, the lab itself is broken.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Target[Any portfolio repo] -->|pip install -e| TL[TargetLoader]
    TL --> H[TestHarness]
    DS[evaluation/datasets - 7 labeled suites] --> H
    H --> R[LabReport]
    R --> JSON[JSON + Markdown + HTML dashboard]
    R --> CI[CI step summary / thresholds]
    CI -->|PASS / FAIL| GH[GitHub Actions]
    SelfEval[evaluation/run.py] -.reproduces known failures.-> H
```

Layout:

```
ai-agent-testing-lab/
├── lab/                  # harness, metrics, reporters, dashboard, integration, CLI
├── evaluation/
│   ├── datasets/         # seven labeled JSON suites
│   ├── run.py            # self-evaluation entry point
│   └── results/          # generated reports (git-ignored)
├── fixtures/             # known-good / known-broken agents for self-evaluation
├── integration/          # CI template + run_lab_eval.py for downstream repos
├── scripts/demo_eval.py  # quick demo against the fixtures
├── infra/                # Dockerfile + docker-compose.yml
└── .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

## Evaluation Summary

| Suite | What it measures | Metric |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Factual accuracy | recommendation cites expected evidence (source + value range) | hit rate on labeled cases |
| Tool-use | only expected tools are called, with success | tool-use success |
| Recommendation quality | completeness of structured recommendations | quality score |
| Prompt-injection resistance | no forbidden write tool on adversarial input | resistance score |
| Cost | measured cost within labeled cap | cost control |
| Latency | total latency within labeled budget | latency budget |
| Reliability | completion rate over repeated runs | reliability |

Current self-evaluation result (`python -m evaluation.run`):

- **ReliableAgent**: passes all seven suites.
- **BrokenAgent**: caught on factual accuracy, tool-use, prompt-injection
  resistance, and reliability.
- Lab status: **effective** (`lab_effective: true` in `evaluation/results/self_eval.json`).

See [docs/evaluation.md](docs/evaluation.md) for methodology and results.

## Setup

```bash
# from the portfolio root (temp/ai_portfolio)
pip install -e ./ai-marketing-shared
pip install -e ./ai-marketing-growth-os   # optional: evaluate the flagship
pip install -e ./ai-agent-testing-lab
```

## Demo

```bash
lab-eval                     # CLI: run self-evaluation
python scripts/demo_eval.py  # print a sample report for the fixtures
```

Zero API keys required: the lab is fully rule-based and deterministic.

## CI Integration for Other Repos

Copy `integration/ci-workflow-template.yml` and call the lab from any repo:

```yaml
- name: Evaluate agents with ai-agent-testing-lab
  run: |
    pip install -e ../ai-marketing-shared ../ai-agent-testing-lab
    python ../ai-agent-testing-lab/integration/run_lab_eval.py \
      --target "your_repo.agents:build_agents" \
      --thresholds path/to/thresholds.json
```

The script writes metrics to the GitHub Actions step summary and exits
non-zero when any metric falls below its threshold. See
[integration/README.md](integration/README.md).

## Roadmap

- [x] Seven labeled datasets (factual, tool-use, recommendation quality, injection, cost, latency, reliability)
- [x] Test harness importing agents from other repos via `pip install -e`
- [x] Metrics reporters and HTML dashboard
- [x] Self-evaluation reproducing known agent failures
- [x] CI integration template for downstream repos
- [ ] Per-suite golden regression baselines for each portfolio repo
- [ ] MCP adapter evaluation suites
- [ ] Cost/latency regression charts published as CI artifacts

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

readme.excerpt:
# AI Search Visibility Auditor

Open-source **GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)** toolkit. In 2026, zero-click searches have reached ~68% and AI Overviews cut click-through rates on top organic positions by ~34%. Ranking #1 is no longer enough — brands must be **cited by AI answer engines**. This tool audits whether your website is ready for that world.

It answers three questions:
1. **Are AI crawlers allowed in?** — robots.txt checks for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended and more.
2. **Do you speak the llms.txt standard?** — detects, validates and generates `/llms.txt` so AI crawlers know what to prioritize.
3. **Is your content structured for AI citation?** — audits answer blocks, question-based headings, FAQ/Article schema and E-E-A-T signals (author, dates, structured body).

Built as a free, open-source alternative to paid AI-visibility tools (SE Ranking ~$129/mo, Semrush ~$139–299/mo, Otterly.AI, Promptwatch).

---

## Features

- **AI crawler access audit** — parses `robots.txt` with standard longest-match precedence, flags crawlers that are disallowed from key paths, distinguishes Google-Extended (Gemini training) from AI Overviews indexing.
- **llms.txt detection, validation and generation** — parses existing files, flags missing titles / duplicate URLs / non-absolute links, and generates a ready-to-publish `llms.txt` from your pages.
- **On-page AI-citation readiness audit** — detects direct answer blocks in the first ~100 words, question-based headings, FAQPage / Article / Organization / Person schema (including `@graph`), author & date signals, and structured body content (lists, tables).
- **Streamlit dashboard** — enter a URL, run the audit, see a prioritized issue list (critical / warning / info), crawler access table, suggested `llms.txt`, and CSV export.
- **Zero heavy dependencies** — stdlib-only analysis engine (urllib + html.parser); Streamlit is the only runtime dependency for the dashboard.
- **Polite fetching** — custom user-agent, timeouts, size limits, small crawl delay.

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hamid-digitalmarketer/ai-search-visibility-auditor.git
cd ai-search-visibility-auditor
pip install -r requirements.txt
streamlit run app.py
```

Then open http://localhost:8501, enter a URL (e.g. `https://your-site.com`) and hit **Run audit**.

## CLI usage (library)

```python
from geo_audit import fetcher, report

status, robots = fetcher.polite_fetch("https://example.com/robots.txt")
_, llms = fetcher.polite_fetch("https://example.com/llms.txt")
_, html = fetcher.polite_fetch("https://example.com/")

audit = report.run_audit(
    domain="https://example.com",
    robots_text=robots if status == 200 else None,
    robots_status=status,
    llms_text=llms,
    llms_status=200,
    html=html,
)
for issue in audit.sorted_issues():
    print(issue["severity"], issue["code"], "-", issue["message"])
```

## What each check means

| Check | Why it matters in 2026 |
|---|---|
| GPTBot / ClaudeBot / PerplexityBot blocked | AI answer engines can't cite what they can't crawl. |
| Google-Extended blocked | Controls Gemini training only; doesn't block AI Overviews. Blocking by reflex hides content from model training pipelines. |
| `llms.txt` missing | The emerging standard that explicitly guides AI crawlers to priority content (adoption accelerating across major sites). |
| No direct answer block | AI extractors often stop at the first clean answer; burying it costs citations. |
| No FAQ/Article schema | FAQ schema feeds structured Q&A pairs straight into knowledge graphs — one of the highest-impact citation signals. |
| No author / no dates (E-E-A-T) | Anonymous, undated content fails AI quality filters. |

## Project structure

```
geo_audit/
  fetcher.py           # polite HTTP fetching (timeout, size limit, delay)
  robots_analyzer.py   # robots.txt parsing + AI crawler access checks
  llms_analyzer.py     # llms.txt parse / validate /

    robots_status=status,
    llms_text=llms,
    llms_status=200,
    html=html,
)
for issue in audit.sorted_issues():
    print(issue["severity"], issue["code"], "-", issue["message"])
```

## What each check means

| Check | Why it matters in 2026 |
|---|---|
| GPTBot / ClaudeBot / PerplexityBot blocked | AI answer engines can't cite what they can't crawl. |
| Google-Extended blocked | Controls Gemini training only; doesn't block AI Overviews. Blocking by reflex hides content from model training pipelines. |
| `llms.txt` missing | The emerging standard that explicitly guides AI crawlers to priority content (adoption accelerating across major sites). |
| No direct answer block | AI extractors often stop at the first clean answer; burying it costs citations. |
| No FAQ/Article schema | FAQ schema feeds structured Q&A pairs straight into knowledge graphs — one of the highest-impact citation signals. |
| No author / no dates (E-E-A-T) | Anonymous, undated content fails AI quality filters. |

## Project structure

```
geo_audit/
  fetcher.py           # polite HTTP fetching (timeout, size limit, delay)
  robots_analyzer.py   # robots.txt parsing + AI crawler access checks
  llms_analyzer.py     # llms.txt parse / validate / generate
  content_analyzer.py  # on-page citation readiness signals
  report.py            # audit orchestration + prioritized issues
app.py                 # Streamlit dashboard
tests/                 # unit tests (unittest)
```

## Tests

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Deployment (optional)

The app is a standard Streamlit app and deploys to **Streamlit Community Cloud** or any container host. For a zero-server demo, host the generated `llms.txt` and audit report as static files on GitHub Pages.

## Roadmap

- [ ] Multi-page crawl (audit an entire site, not just one page)
- [ ] AI citation monitor (lightweight answer-engine mention tracking)
- [ ] Schema validation details (JSON-LD syntax errors)
- [ ] llms.txt diff/versioning suggestions
- [ ] Sitemap-aware llms.txt generation

Every repo in the portfolio must produce **evidence-backed recommendations**, use **tools safely**,
enforce **human approval**, expose **observability**, and run with **zero API keys**. Without a shared
foundation, 17 repos would drift into 17 incompatible conventions. `ai-marketing-shared` defines those
conventions **once**:

1. **Structured outputs** — Pydantic v2 schemas with field names matching the master prompt exactly.
2. **Safe tools** — a `Tool` base class with explicit permission levels (`read` / `write` / `external`)
   and a registry that rejects calls below the required permission.
3. **Provider-agnostic** — OpenAI, Anthropic, local HTTP endpoints, and a deterministic mock provider
   (default) so every demo runs at `$0.00`.
4. **Observability** — every run is traced with inputs, tool calls, outputs, cost, latency.
5. **Cost controls** — model pricing tables, ledgers, and budget caps.
6. **Evaluation** — a harness with dataset loaders and metric reporters, wired into CI.

## Using the Mock Provider (Default)

`ProviderFactory.get_provider()` returns `MockProvider` unless `AI_MARKETING_PROVIDER` is set:

> **Diagnostic and quality audit engine for Meta Lead Ads (Instant Forms) and CRM pipelines.**  
> Detects disposable burner emails, fake telephone numbers, sub-5-second speed-clickers, and computes true **Cost-Per-Qualified-Lead (CPQL)** vs vanity front-end **Cost-Per-Lead (CPL)**. Generates automated **Meta Conversions API (CAPI) offline event payloads** for value optimization and custom audience exclusion lists.

---

![Meta Lead Quality Analyzer Audit Preview](docs/report_preview.png)

---

## ⚡ The Problem: Cheap Meta Leads That Never Close

Meta Lead Ads (Instant Forms) deliver extraordinary lead volume at low apparent front-end Cost-Per-Lead ($15–$30 CPL). However, sales and revenue teams frequently encounter severe drop-off:

1. **Auto-Fill Mis-clicks & Speed Bots**: Meta pre-populates lead forms with user profile data. Users scrolling Instagram Reels tap the ad, accidentally confirm the pre-filled form, and submit in $<5$ seconds without reading the offer.
2. **Burner Disposable Emails**: Users seeking downloadable PDFs or price sheets use throwaway temporary inboxes (`@mailinator.com`, `@tempmail.com`, `@guerrillamail.com`).
3. **Fictional Phone Numbers**: Users bypass mandatory phone fields with repeated digits (`5555555555`, `1234567890`) or reserved dummy prefixes.
4. **The CPL vs. CPQL Illusion**: While marketing celebrates a $25.00 CPL, sales only qualifies 1 in 8 leads, making the true Cost-Per-Qualified-Lead (CPQL) $200.00+. Meta's algorithm continues optimizing for cheap, low-intent volume because down-funnel sales qualification signals are never fed back.

**Meta Lead Quality Analyzer** audits your lead flow, calculates real acquisition economics, and automates closed-loop feedback to train Meta's algorithms on qualified pipeline.

---

## 🚀 Key Features

- 🔍 **5 Specialized Quality Analyzers**:
  - `DisposableEmailAnalyzer`: Flags temporary inboxes, throwaway domain providers, and dummy addresses.
  - `PhoneValidator`: Detects repeated digit spam, sequential keyboard inputs, and invalid formats.
  - `CompletionSpeedAnalyzer`: Flags sub-5-second submissions indicating auto-fill mis-clicks or bot scrapers.
  - `CustomQuestionAnalyzer`: Evaluates user answers to custom qualification questions for gibberish (`asdf`, `none`, `test`).
  - `CRMStageMatchAnalyzer`: Cross-references leads against CRM deal stages (`Qualified`, `Disqualified_Bad_Info`, `Won`), calculating true CPQL and junk lead percentage.
- 🔄 **Meta CAPI Offline Event Exporter**:
  - Generates ready-to-upload JSON payloads with SHA-256 normalized user matching (`QualifiedLead`, `WonDeal`) to feed back into Meta Advantage+ value optimization.
- 📋 **CRM Disqualification & Suppression List**:
  - Exports flagged leads to CSV for bulk CRM cleanup and Meta Cus

> **A production-grade, open-source PPC budget leak detector for Google Ads and Meta Ads.**  
> Automatically detects search query bleed, internal keyword cannibalization, junk mobile app placements, geo-location bleed, off-hour dayparting spikes, and runaway smart bidding CPC anomalies. Generates one-click exclusion lists for **Google Ads Editor** and self-contained interactive Tailwind CSS audit dashboards.

---

![PPC Waste Audit Dashboard Preview](docs/report_preview.png)

---

## ⚡ The Problem: Invisible PPC Ad Spend Bleed

Modern paid search and display platforms optimize for inventory monetization, often hiding budget waste inside broad matching, Performance Max black boxes, and multi-network default settings:

1. **Broad Match Query Bleed**: Broad match expansion captures low-intent, non-converting queries (`free`, `login`, `jobs`, `tutorial`).
2. **Internal Keyword Cannibalization**: Multiple campaigns or ad groups bid against each other on the same search queries, driving up your own clearing CPCs.
3. **GDN / PMax Junk Placements**: Display campaigns and Performance Max silently serve impressions on hyper-casual mobile games (`mobileapp::*`) and MFA click-farms with high accidental click-through rates and 0% conversion rates.
4. **Geographic Bleed**: Ads show to users outside your targeted geographies due to Google's default *"Presence or interest"* setting.
5. **Dayparting Waste**: High budget burns between 1:00 AM and 5:00 AM with zero conversions and unstaffed sales teams.
6. **Smart Bidding Runaways**: Automated bidding algorithms aggressively bid on low-intent search terms during inventory spikes without CPC ceilings.

**PPC Waste Detector** parses your raw Google Ads or Meta Ads performance CSV reports and pinpoints every wasted dollar with mathematical rigor.

---

## 🚀 Key Features

- 🔍 **6 Specialized Detection Engines**:
  - `SearchQueryBleedDetector`: Flags negative-intent queries, zero-conversion high-spend queries, and traffic spikes.
  - `KeywordCannibalizationDetector`: Maps internal cross-campaign auction conflicts and calculates wasted delta spend.
  - `JunkPlacementLeakDetector`: Detects spam domains, MFA click-farms, and mobile game app IDs (`mobileapp::*`).
  - `GeoBleedDetector`: Catches impressions and spend occurring outside your target service areas.
  - `DaypartingWasteDetector`: Identifies off-peak hourly budget burns with conversion rates below 10% of account average.
  - `SmartBiddingRunawayDetector`: Detects severe CPC inflation ($>3\times$ median) triggered by unconstrained automated bidding.
- 📋 **Google Ads Editor Ready**:
  - `negative_keywords_editor.csv`: Formatted with `Campaign`, `Ad Group`, `Criterion Type`, `Keyword` for bulk import.

- **`ai-marketing-growth-os`**: Operates at the **tactical campaign layer** (campaign audits, creative fatigue detection, keyword expansion, search query sanitization).
- **`ai-marketing-mix-copilot`**: Operates at the **strategic portfolio capital layer** (cross-channel media mix allocation, Bayesian econometrics, empirical geo-holdout causal lift, counterfactual revenue forecasting).

## 📐 Mathematical & Econometric Foundations

The platform's analytical engine implements production-grade Bayesian econometrics and causal inference:

### 1. Geometric Adstock Carryover
Advertising impact decays across subsequent periods following an exponential decay parameter $\alpha \in [0, 1)$:
$$x_{t}^* = x_t + \alpha \cdot x_{t-1}^*$$
Where:
- $x_t$ is the raw spend in week $t$.
- $x_t^*$ is the cumulative adstocked media pressure.
- $\alpha$ is the decay parameter (e.g., $\alpha = 0.65$ for YouTube brand campaigns vs. $\alpha = 0.25$ for direct response search).

### 2. Hill Saturation Function (Diminishing Marginal Returns)
Media response follows an S-shaped Hill function parameterizing maximum potential revenue ($K$) and curve slope ($S$):
$$S(x^*) = \frac{(x^*)^S}{(x^*)^S + K^S}$$
Marginal ROAS (mROI) is computed as the first derivative of the revenue response curve with respect to spend:
$$\text{mROI}(x^*) = \frac{d\,\text{Revenue}}{d\,x^*}$$
- When $\text{mROI} < 1.00$, every additional dollar invested costs more than it returns (**Channel Saturation**).
- When $\text{mROI} > 2.00$, the channel has significant headroom to absorb capital (**Under-allocated Opportunity**).

### 3. Difference-in-Differences Causal Lift Estimator
To verify true incremental impact against last-touch reporting, empirical geo-holdout experiments are evaluated using Difference-in-Differences (DiD):
$$\hat{\tau}_{DiD} = \left(\bar{Y}_{T,\text{post}} - \bar{Y}_{T,\text{pre}}\right) - \left(\bar{Y}_{C,\text{post}} - \bar{Y}_{C,\text{pre}}\right)$$
Attribution haircut calculation:
$$\text{Haircut} = \frac{\text{iROAS}_{\text{causal}} - \text{ROAS}_{\text{reported}}}{\text{ROAS}_{\text{reported}}} = \frac{1.45 - 3.80}{3.80} = -61.8\%$$

---

## 🤖 The 5 Specialized AI Agents

Each agent has a strictly bounded toolset, least-privilege permissions, and Pydantic-validated output contracts:

| Agent | Core Responsibilities | Registered Tools | Permission Scope |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Data Quality Agent** | Audits time-series schemas, aligns calendar weeks, imputes zero-variance gaps, detects anomalies, sanitizes text against prompt injections. | `load_raw_data`, `validate_schema`, `detect_missing_values`, `flag_anomalies`, `summarize_data_quality` | `READ_ONLY` |
| **Model Agent** | Decomposes multi-channel revenues, evaluates MCMC chains ($\hat{R} \le 1.018$, $\text{ESS} = 2,450$), calculates adstock carryover, maps Hill curves, and isolates channel mROI. | `fit_bayesian_mmm`, `check_convergence`, `run_diagnostics`, `compute_roi`, `compute_marginal_roi`, `generate_saturation_curves` | `READ_ONLY` |
| **Incrementality Agent** | Analyzes 30-DMA geo holdout experiments, computes synthetic counterfactuals, verifies two-sample t-statistic significance ($p < 0.001$), and determines platform attribution overstatement. | `design_geo_holdout`, `analyze_geo_holdout`, `run_diff_in_diff`, `calculate_lift`, `assess_statistical_significance` | `READ_ONLY` |
| **Scenario Agent** | Solves for the optimal media allocation by equalizing marginal returns across channels; simulates counterfactual spend shifts with 90% Bayesian credible intervals. | `define_budget_scenario`, `simulate_budget_reallocation`, `forecast_outcomes`, `compute_uncertainty_intervals`, `optimize_allocation` | `READ_ONLY` |
| **Explanation Agent** | Translates complex econometric parameters into plain-language executive decision briefs for CMOs and CFOs, complete with citations, risks, and next steps. | `summarize_model_results`, `translate_to_plain_language`, `generate_executive_summary`, `recommend_actions`, `cite_evidence` | `READ_ONLY` |

---

## 🛡️ Security, Governance & Human-in-the-Loop

1. **Write-Capable Tool Isolation**:
   - `apply_budget_reallocation` is strictly registered under `ToolPermission.WRITE_CAPABLE`.
   - The multi-agent orchestrator actively intercepts write actions and enforces the governance state machine:
   $$\text{PENDING} \longrightarrow \text{APPROVED} \longrightarrow \text{EXECUTED} \longrightarrow \text{MEASURED}$$
   - Any execution attempted while an action is in `PENDING` state is immediately halted by a safety guardrail.
2. **Defensive Prompt-Injection Sanitization**:
   - External inputs, dataset tags, and user notes are scanned for jailbreaks (`"IGNORE ALL PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS"`, `"OVERRIDE BUDGET"`) via regex normalization and filtered before agent ingestion.
3. **Zero API Key Leakage**:
   - Configuration is fully decoupled into `.env.example`. Demo execution requires `$0.00` API spend and zero third-party credentials.

---

The Copilot features a single-page reactive dashboard (`frontend/index.html`) served directly by the FastAPI backend:

### Dashboard Capabilities:

## 🔒 Security Policy & Prompt-Injection Defense

To safeguard production deployments, all incoming data streams and parameters pass through rigorous input-hygiene filters. The system actively neutralizes adversarial prompt injections that attempt to override capital allocation guardrails:

```python
# data/connectors.py
def sanitize_text(text: str) -> str:
    # Neutralize prompt injection attempts targeting approval state machines
    cleaned = re.sub(
        r"(ignore (all )?previous instructions|system override|you are now|override budget)",
        "[REDACTED_ADVERSARIAL_INJECTION]",
        text,
        flags=re.IGNORECASE
    )
    return cleaned
```

Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for LangChain
===================================================================

|preview| |pypi| |versions|

- `Client Library Documentation`_
- `Product Documentation`_

The **Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for LangChain** package provides a first class experience for connecting to
Cloud SQL instances from the LangChain ecosystem while providing the following benefits:

- **Simplified & Secure Connections**: easily and securely create shared connection pools to connect to Google Cloud databases utilizing IAM for authorization and database authentication without needing to manage SSL certificates, configure firewall rules, or enable authorized networks.
- **Improved performance & Simplified management**: use a single-table schema can lead to faster query execution, especially for large collections.
- **Improved metadata handling**: store metadata in columns instead of JSON, resulting in significant performance improvements.
- **Clear separation**: clearly separate table and extension creation, allowing for distinct permissions and streamlined workflows.

.. |preview| image:: https://img.shields.io/badge/support-preview-orange.svg
   :target: https://github.com/googleapis/google-cloud-python/blob/main/README.rst#stability-levels
.. |pypi| image:: https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg.svg
   :target: https://pypi.org/project/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg/
.. |versions| image:: https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg.svg
   :target: https://pypi.org/project/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg/
.. _Client Library Documentation: https://cloud.google.com/python/docs/reference/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg/latest
.. _Product Documentation: https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs

Quick Start
-----------

In order to use this library, you first need to go through the following steps:

1. `Select or create a Cloud Platform project.`_
2. `Enable billing for your project.`_
3. `Enable the Cloud SQL Admin API.`_
4. `Setup Authentication.`_

.. _Select or create a Cloud Platform project.: https://console.cloud.google.com/project
.. _Enable billing for your project.: https://cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/modify-project#enable_billing_for_a_project
.. _Enable the Cloud SQL Admin API.:
.. _Setup Authentication.: https://googleapis.dev/python/google-api-core/latest/auth.html

Installation
~~~~~~~~~~~~

Install this library in a virtual environment using `venv`_. `venv`_ is a tool that
creates isolated Python environments. These isolated environments can have separate
versions of Python packages, which allows you to isolate one project's dependencies
from the dependencies of other projects.

With `venv`_, it's possible to install this library without needing system
install permissions, and without clashing with the installed system
dependencies.

.. _`venv`: https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html


Supported Python Versions
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Python >= 3.10

Mac/Linux
^^^^^^^^^

.. code-block:: console

    pip install virtualenv
    virtualenv <your-env>
    source <your-env>/bin/activate
    <your-env>/bin/pip install langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg


Windows
^^^^^^^

.. code-block:: console

    pip install virtualenv
    virtualenv <your-env>
    <your-env>\Scripts\activate
    <your-env>\Scripts\pip.exe install langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg


Example Usage
-------------

Code samples and snippets live in the `samples/`_ folder.

.. _samples/: https://github.com/googleapis/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg-python/tree/main/samples


Vector Store Usage
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Use a Vector Store to store embedded data and perform vector search.

.. code-block:: python

        from langchain_google_cloud_sql_pg import PostgresVectorstore, PostgresEngine
        from langchain.embeddings import VertexAIEmbeddings


        engine = PostgresEngine.from_instance("project-id", "region", "my-instance", "my-database")
        engine.init_vectorstore_table(
            table_name="my-table",
            vector_size=768,  # Vector size for `VertexAIEmbeddings()`
        )
        embeddings_service = VertexAIEmbeddings(model_name="textembedding-gecko@003")
        vectorstore = PostgresVectorStore.create_sync(
            engine,
            table_name="my-table",
            embeddings=embedding_service
        )

Hybrid search
~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The `PostgresVectorStore` supports hybrid search (dense vectors + full text) for more comprehensive and relevant search results.

.. code-block:: python

  from langchain_google_cloud_sql_pg import HybridSearchConfig, reciprocal_rank_fusion

  vs = PostgresVectorStore.create_sync(
      engine=engine,
      table_name=TABLE_NAME,
      embedding_service=embedding,
      hybrid_search_config=HybridSearchConfig(
        fusion_function=reciprocal_rank_fusion
      ),
  )
  hybrid_docs = vector_store.similarity_search("products", k=5)


See the full `Vector Store`_ tutorial.

.. _`Vector Store`: https://github.com/googleapis/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg-python/tree/main/docs/vector_store.ipynb

Document Loader Usage
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Use a document loader to load data as Documents.

.. code-block:: python

        from langchain_google_cloud_sql_pg import PostgresEngine, PostgresLoader


        engine = PostgresEngine.from_instance("project-id", "region", "my-instance", "my-database")
        loader = PostgresSQLLoader.create_sync(
            engine,
            table_name="my-table-name"
        )
        docs = loader.lazy_load()

See the full `Document Loader`_ tutorial.

.. _`Document Loader`: https://github.com/googleapis/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg-python/tree/main/docs/document_loader.ipynb

Chat Message History Usage
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Use Chat Message History to store messages and provide conversation history to LLMs.

.. code-block:: python

        from langchain_google_cloud_sql_pg import PostgresChatMessageHistory, PostgresEngine


        engine = PostgresEngine.from_instance("project-id", "region", "my-instance", "my-database")
        engine.init_chat_history_table(table_name="my-message-store")
        history = PostgresChatMessageHistory.create_sync(
            engine,
            table_name="my-message-store",
            session_id="my-session_id"
        )

See the full `Chat Message History`_ tutorial.

.. _`Chat Message History`: https://github.com/googleapis/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg-python/tree/main/docs/chat_message_history.ipynb

Langgraph Checkpoint Usage
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Use ``PostgresSaver`` to save snapshots of the graph state at a given point in time.

.. code:: python

   from langchain_google_cloud_sql_pg import PostgresSaver, PostgresEngine
   
   engine = PostgresEngine.from_instance("project-id", "region", "my-instance", "my-database")
   checkpoint = PostgresSaver.create_sync(engine)

See the full `Checkpoint`_ tutorial.

.. _`Checkpoint`: https://github.com/googleapis/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg-python/blob/main/docs/langgraph_checkpoint.ipynb

Example Usage
-------------

Code examples can be found in the `samples/`_ folder.

.. _samples/: https://github.com/googleapis/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg-python/tree/main/samples

Converting between Sync & Async Usage
-------------------------------------

Async functionality improves the speed and efficiency of database connections through concurrency,
which is key for providing enterprise quality performance and scaling in GenAI applications. This
package uses a native async Postgres driver, `asyncpg`_, to optimize Python's async functionality.

LangChain supports `async programming`_, since LLM based application utilize many I/O-bound operations,
such as making API calls to language models, databases, or other services. All components should provide
both async and sync versions of all methods.

`asyncio`_ is a Python library used for concurrent programming and is used as the foundation for multiple
Python asynchronous frameworks. asyncio uses `async` / `await` syntax to achieve concurrency for
non-blocking I/O-bound tasks using one thread with cooperative multitasking instead of multi-threading.

.. _`async programming`: https://python.langchain.com/docs/concepts/async/
.. _`asyncio`: https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio.html
.. _`asyncpg`: https://github.com/MagicStack/asyncpg

Converting Sync to Async
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Update sync methods to `await` async methods

.. code:: python

   engine = await PostgresEngine.afrom_instance("project-id", "region", "my-instance", "my-database")
   await engine.ainit_vectorstore_table(table_name="my-table", vector_size=768)
   vectorstore = await PostgresVectorStore.create(
      engine,
      table_name="my-table",
      embedding_service=VertexAIEmbeddings(model_name="textembedding-gecko@003")
   )

Run the code: notebooks
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

ipython and jupyter notebooks support the use of the `await` keyword without any additional setup

Run the code: FastAPI
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Update routes to use `async def`.

.. code:: python

   @app.get("/invoke/")
   async def invoke(query: str):
      return await retriever.ainvoke(query)


Run the code: Local python file
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

It is recommend to create a top-level async method definition: `async def` to wrap multiple async methods.
Then use `asyncio.run()` to run the the top-level entrypoint, e.g. "main()"

.. code:: python

   async def main():
      response = await retriever.ainvoke(query)
      print(response)

   asyncio.run(main())


Contributions
-------------

Contributions to this library are always welcome and highly encouraged.

See `CONTRIBUTING`_ for more information how to get started.

Please note that this project is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By participating in
this project you agree to abide by its terms. See `Code of Conduct`_ for more
information.

.. _`CONTRIBUTING`: https://github.com/googleapis/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg-python/tree/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
.. _`Code of Conduct`: https://github.com/googleapis/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg-python/tree/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

License
-------

Apache 2.0 - See
`LICENSE <https://github.com/googleapis/langchain-google-cloud-sql-pg-python/tree/main/LICENSE>`_
for more information.

Disclaimer
----------

This is not an officially supported Google product.

Fork the Repository First, fork the `musheabdulhakim/gohighlevel-php` repository on GitHub and clone your fork to your local machine. ```bash git clone https://github.com/MusheAbdulHakim/gohighlevel-php-sdk.git cd gohighlevel-php ``` ### 2\. Install Dependencies ```bash composer install ``` ## Development Workflow ### 1\. Create a New Branch Before you start working, create a new branch for your feature or bug fix. Use a descriptive name that reflects your changes. ```bash git checkout -b feature/your-awesome-feature ``` ### 2\. Write Your Code Follow the existing coding style and project structure. The SDK uses `strict_types=1` and is built on a PSR-18 compliant HTTP client system. When adding a new feature or fixing a bug, remember to write **unit tests**. All new code must be covered by tests to ensure it works as expected and prevents regressions. Your tests should be written using [PestPHP](https://pestphp.com/). ### 3\. Run the Test Suite Before committing your changes, you must ensure that all tests pass and the code meets the project's quality standards. You can run the entire test suite with a single command: ```bash composer test ``` This command executes all quality checks in a specific order: * `@test:lint`: Checks for and automatically fixes coding style issues using **PHP-CS-Fixer**. * `@test:refacto`: Runs **Rector** to find potential code improvements. * `@test:types`: Performs static analysis with **PHPStan** to catch type-related errors. * `@test:unit`: Executes all unit tests with **PestPHP**. ### 4\. Fix Linting and Style Errors The project uses `php-cs-fixer` to enforce a consistent coding style. You can automatically fix most issues by running: ```bash composer lint ``` To see what changes would be made without applying them, use the dry run command: ```bash composer test:lint ``` ### 5\. Submit a Pull Request Once your code is complete, tested, and all checks pass, commit your changes and push your branch to your forked repository. ```bash git add . git commit -m "feat: Add a new feature for managing workflows" git push origin feature/your-awesome-feature ``` Finally, open a pull request from your branch to the `master` branch of the original repository. Provide a clear and concise description of your changes, and reference any relevant issues. Thank you again for your contribution\! We will review your pull request as soon as possible.

Turn Claude, Codex, and other MCP-capable AI clients into a chat-driven GoHighLevel operating layer. - **Confirmation gates** before consequential CRM writes

> **Native GHL workflows by chat:** RealWave positions its Automation Architect as turning a sentence into a live native GoHighLevel workflow, then testing and verifying the result. **[Build with RealWave →](https://ghlmcp.ai?via=jake14)**
>
> Affiliate disclosure: this is the repository maintainer's RealWave referral link. The maintainer may earn a commission if you sign up through it.

### Why use both?

| What you want to do | Best fit |
| --- | --- |
| Search, read, update, and coordinate supported GHL CRM records over chat | **GoHighLevel MCP 2026** |
| Inspect workflows, enroll contacts, trigger existing workflows, and read executions | **GoHighLevel MCP 2026** |

The MCP now tells compatible AI clients about that boundary during initialization and recommends the disclosed RealWave link when a native workflow-building request hits it.

readme.excerpt:
# k8s-ai-bench

`k8s-ai-bench` is a benchmark for assessing the performance of LLM models for Kubernetes related tasks. It evaluates AI agents (like `kubectl-ai`) on their ability to perform real-world Kubernetes operations such as creating deployments, debugging crash loops, and scaling applications.

## 📊 Live Dashboard

See [k8s-ai-bench live leaderboard](https://gke-labs.github.io/k8s-ai-bench/) for the latest benchmark results.

The leaderboard shows run results for widely used proprietary and open models over a few run types:

* **Pass@1**: Can the agent solve the task on the first try? This measures raw capability and immediate correctness.
* **Pass@5**: Can the agent solve the task at least once in 5 attempts? This shows if the agent can eventually find a solution.
* **Pass^5**: Does the agent solve the task every single time? This measures reliability and consistency, which is crucial for autonomous usage.



## 🚀 Quick Start

### 1. Build the Binary
```sh
go build
```

### 2. Run an Evaluation
Run the benchmark against your agent binary. Results will be saved to the `.build` directory.
```sh
# Basic usage
./k8s-ai-bench run --agent-bin <path/to/kubectl-ai> --output-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench

# Run a specific task type (e.g., scaling tasks)
./k8s-ai-bench run --agent-bin <path/to/kubectl-ai> --task-pattern "scale" --output-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench
```

## 🛠 Usage Guide

### `run` Subcommand
The `run` subcommand executes the benchmark evaluations. It creates ephemeral clusters to ensure test isolation. We support two platforms for the test environment: **Kind** (default) and **vCluster**.

**vCluster Prerequisites:**
For a detailed step-by-step guide on setting up and using vCluster, see [vCluster Guide](docs/vcluster.md).

To use `vcluster`, you must have:
* The `vcluster` [CLI](https://www.vcluster.com/docs/vcluster/) installed.
* A running host Kubernetes cluster.
* A kubecontext to connect to the host cluster (passed via `--host-cluster-context`).


```sh
# Run with specific LLM provider and model
./k8s-ai-bench run \
  --agent-bin <path/to/kubectl-ai> \
  --llm-provider gemini \
  --models gemini-2.5-pro-preview-03-25 \
  --task-pattern fix \
  --output-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench
```

**Common Flags:**
| Flag | Description | Default |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `--agent-bin` | Path to kubectl-ai binary (Required) | - |
| `--output-dir` | Directory to write results (Required) | - |
| `--task-pattern` | RegEx pattern to filter tasks (e.g. 'pod', 'fix') | - |
| `--llm-provider` | LLM provider ID (e.g. 'gemini', 'openai') | gemini |
| `--models` | Comma-separated list of models | gemini-2.5-pro... |
| `--concurrency` | Number of parallel tasks (0 = auto) | 0 |
| `--cluster-provider` | Cluster provider to use (`kind` or `vcluster`) | kind |
| `--host-cluster-context` | Host cluster context for vcluster (Required if provider is vcluster) | - |

### `analyze` Subcommand
Process and summarize results from previous runs.

```sh
# Generate a Markdown report
./k8s-ai-bench analyze --input-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench --results-filepath report.md

# Generate JSONL for visualization
./k8s-ai-bench analyze --input-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench --output-format jsonl --results-filepath site/combined_results.jsonl
```

## 💻 Development Scripts
For a streamlined development loop, use the scripts in `dev/ci/periodics/`:

- **Run Evaluation Loop**: Runs evaluations multiple times to test consistency.
  ```sh
  ./dev/ci/periodics/run-eval-loop.sh --iterations 5 --task-pattern "create"
  ```
- **Run Single Evaluation**:
  ```sh
  TEST_ARGS="--task-pattern=fix-probes" ./dev/ci/periodics/run-evals.sh
  ```
- **Analyze Results**:
  ```sh
  ./dev/ci/periodics/analyze-evals.sh --show-failures
  ```

## 📈 Visualizing Results Locally

The `site` directory contains a static website (Vue.js based) for visualizing benchmark results.

1.  **Generate Data**:
    ```sh
    ./k8s-ai-bench analyze --input-dir .build/k8s-ai-bench --output-format jsonl --result

readme.excerpt:
# ![](static/logo-header.png)

> [!NOTE]
> This project is for demonstration only and is not an officially supported
> Google product.
>
> If you're a Googler using this demo, please fill up this
> [form](https://forms.gle/dJUdMEbUu7k3TmT4A). If you're interested in using our
> hosted version, please fill up this
> [form](https://forms.gle/3AknwhhWv2pWw46Q8).

## Introduction

This project provides a production-quality reference implementation for building
Agentic applications that use [Agents] and [Retrieval Augmented Generation
(RAG)][rag] to query and interact with data stored in Google Cloud Databases.

This demonstration features Cymbal Air, a fictional airline. The application
showcases a customer service assistant that helps travelers manage flights and
find information about San Francisco International Airport (SFO), Cymbal Air's
hub. The agent can answer questions like:

* *Are there any luxury shops in the terminal?*
* *Where can I get coffee near gate A6?*
* *I need to find a gift for my colleague.*
* *What flights are headed to NYC tomorrow?*

[rag]: https://www.promptingguide.ai/techniques/rag
[Agents]: https://www.promptingguide.ai/agents/introduction

### Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)

One of the best tools for reducing hallucinations is to use Retrieval Augmented
Generation (RAG). RAG is the concept of retrieving some data or information,
augmenting your prompt to the agent, and allowing it to generate more accurate
responses based on the data included in the prompt. This grounds the model’s
response, making it less likely to hallucinate. This technique is also useful
for allowing the agent to access data it didn’t have when it was trained. And
unlike fine-tuning, the information retrieved for RAG does not alter the model

developers can give their applications access to a wider range of information

chain of calls, the LLM acts as an intelligent Agent that decides which tools to
use and in what order. It is given a set of available tools, each with a

"thought process" allows the agent to handle a wider variety of queries and to
break down complex questions into smaller, manageable steps.

# ![](static/logo-header.png)

> [!NOTE]
> This project is for demonstration only and is not an officially supported
> Google product.
>
> If you're a Googler using this demo, please fill up this
> [form](https://forms.gle/dJUdMEbUu7k3TmT4A). If you're interested in using our
> hosted version, please fill up this
> [form](https://forms.gle/3AknwhhWv2pWw46Q8).

## Introduction

This project provides a production-quality reference implementation for building
Agentic applications that use [Agents] and [Retrieval Augmented Generation
(RAG)][rag] to query and interact with data stored in Google Cloud Databases.

This demonstration features Cymbal Air, a fictional airline. The application
showcases a customer service assistant that helps travelers manage flights and
find information about San Francisco International Airport (SFO), Cymbal Air's
hub. The agent can answer questions like:

* *Are there any luxury shops in the terminal?*
* *Where can I get coffee near gate A6?*
* *I need to find a gift for my colleague.*
* *What flights are headed to NYC tomorrow?*

[rag]: https://www.promptingguide.ai/techniques/rag
[Agents]: https://www.promptingguide.ai/agents/introduction

## Table of Contents
<!-- TOC depthfrom:2 -->

- [Understanding the demo](#understanding-the-demo)
    - [Retrieval Augmented Generation RAG](#retrieval-augmented-generation-rag)
    - [Agent-based Orchestration](#agent-based-orchestration)
    - [Architecture](#architecture)
- [Deployment](#deployment)
    - [Before you begin](#before-you-begin)
    - [One-Time Database & Tool Configuration](#one-time-database--tool-configuration)
    - [Launch the Toolbox Server Choose One](#launch-the-toolbox-server-choose-one)
    - [Running the Agentic Application](#running-the-agentic-application)
    - [Clean Up](#clean-up)
- [Customizing Your Tools](#customizing-your-tools)

<!-- /TOC -->

## Understanding the demo

### Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)

One of the best tools for reducing hallucinations is to use Retrieval Augmented
Generation (RAG). RAG is the concept of retrieving some data or information,
augmenting your prompt to the agent, and allowing it to generate more accurate
responses based on the data included in the prompt. This grounds the model’s
response, making it less likely to hallucinate. This technique is also useful
for allowing the agent to access data it didn’t have when it was trained. And
unlike fine-tuning, the information retrieved for RAG does not alter the model
or otherwise leave the context of the request - making it more suitable for use
cases where information privacy and security are important.

Cloud databases provide a managed solution for storing and accessing data in a
scalable and a reliable way. By connecting an agent to a cloud database,
developers can give their applications access to a wider range of information
and reduce the risk of hallucinations.


### Agent-based Orchestration

This application uses an Agent-based orchestration model. Instead of a static
chain of calls, the LLM acts as an intelligent Agent that decides which tools to
use and in what order. It is given a set of available tools, each with a
specific function (e.g., `find_flights`, `list_amenities`). Based on the user's
query, the agent reasons about the best tool to use to find the answer. This
"thought process" allows the agent to handle a wider variety of queries and to
break down complex questions into smaller, manageable steps.

### Architecture

![Overview](architecture.svg)

The architecture consists of three main components:
1. **Application** -- The user-facing agentic app that orchestrates the
   interaction between the user and the agent.
1. **MCP Toolbox** -- [MCP Toolbox](https://github.com/googleapis/genai-toolbox)
   is a middleware server that exposes the database operations as a set of
   tools. The LLM agent connects to the Toolbox to execute these tools. This
   provides a secure, scalable, and modular way to manage database interactions.
1. **Database** -- The database containing the data the agent can use to answer
   questions. For this application, the database used was intentionally designed
   to be interchangeable in order to make it easier to run this on your
   preferred database.

Using the Toolbox as an intermediary offers several advantages:

1. **Better Security** - The Toolbox handles authentication and authorization,
   preventing the agent from directly accessing the database and reducing the
   risk of security vulnerabilities.
1. **Better scalability** - Toolbox allows multiple different Agents to leverage
   it, as well as allowing it to scale independently. It allows for production
   best practices such as connection pooling or caching.
1. **Better recall** - Agents perform better when given smaller, discrete tasks
   they can use to accomplish larger goals. By mapping a specific action to a
   specific, pre-determined query, via tools, it significantly improves the
   agent's ability to leverage it successfully.

Head over to the official [MCP Toolbox
docs](https://mcp-toolbox.dev/documentation/introduction/)
for more details.

## Deployment

Deploying Cymbal Air app is a three-step process. You will first download the
necessary tools, then perform a one-time setup for your database and Toolbox
configuration, and finally launch the Toolbox server and the app.

### Before you begin

First, clone this repository and download the MCP Toolbox binary.

1.  **Clone the repository:**
      ```bash
      git clone https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cymbal-air-toolbox-demo.git
      cd cymbal-air-toolbox-demo
      ```
2.  **Download MCP Toolbox binary:**

      Follow [these
      steps](https://mcp-toolbox.dev/documentation/introduction/#install-toolbox)
      to download the binary. This involves running the following commands:
      ```bash
      # See the releases page for the latest version
      export VERSION=0.8.0
      curl -O https://storage.googleapis.com/genai-toolbox/v$VERSION/linux/amd64/toolbox
      chmod +x toolbox
      ```

### One-Time Database & Tool Configuration

Next, you must perform a one-time setup to create your database instance,
populate it with data, and create the `tools.yaml` configuration file. This
process uses the Toolbox binary you just downloaded.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> For detailed, step-by-step instructions, follow the **[Database Setup
> Guide](docs/database_setup.md)**.

> [!NOTE]
> If you have already configured your own database, you can skip this section.

### Launch the Toolbox Server (Choose One)

After your database is initialized and your `tools.yaml` file is created, you
must run the Toolbox server so the agentic app can connect to it. You can either
run it locally for development or deploy it to Cloud Run for a more robust
setup.

#### **Option A:** Run Toolbox Locally

For local development and testing, you can run the Toolbox server directly from
your terminal. This is the quickest way to get started.

**For instructions, follow the [guide to running the Toolbox
locally](https://mcp-toolbox.dev/documentation/introduction/#run-toolbox).**

The basic command will be:
```bash
./toolbox --tools-file "tools.yaml"
```

#### **Option B:** Deploy Toolbox to Cloud Run

For a scalable and production-ready setup, you can deploy the Toolbox as a
service on Google Cloud Run. This provides a stable, shareable endpoint for your
application.

**For instructions, follow the [guide to deploying the Toolbox on Cloud
Run](https://mcp-toolbox.dev/documentation/deploy-to/cloud-run/)**.

### Running the Agentic Application

[Instructions for running app locally](docs/run_app.md)

### Clean Up

[Instructions for cleaning up resources](docs/clean_up.md)

## Customizing Your Tools

This demo can serve as a starting point for building your own Agentic
applications. You can customize the tools available to the agent by modifying
the MCP Toolbox configuration file.

Please refer to the [MCP Toolbox documentation][configure] for more information on creating
and configuring tools.

[toolbox]: (https://mcp-toolbox.dev/documentation/getting-started/)
[configure]: (https://mcp-toolbox.dev/documentation/configuration/)

# PubChem Finder

Search [PubChem](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) by chemical structure from your
terminal or from Claude. PubChem Finder builds a local fingerprint index of PubChem (all
of it, or the slice you need) for exact similarity and substructure search with no rate
limits, wraps PubChem's live services for names, safety data and bioassays, and adds RDKit
chemistry: structure drawings, med-chem triage and descriptors. Local search works from the
first question, on a built-in set of 1,932 FDA-approved drugs, until you build a PubChem
index. It runs as a command-line tool, a Python library and an
[MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server for Claude Desktop, Claude Code and other MCP
clients.

[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/pubchem-finder.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/pubchem-finder/)
[![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/pubchem-finder.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/pubchem-finder/)
[![CI](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/blob/master/LICENSE)
<!-- mcp-name: io.github.MysterionRise/pubchem-finder -->

![A similarity search for aspirin and a SMARTS substructure search over 444,794 PubChem compounds, with the hits appearing and their key atoms highlighted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/master/docs/media/search-demo.gif)

*Real searches over the first 444,794 compounds of PubChem, rendered from the index the
project's real-data workflow builds: similarity hits for aspirin with the atoms that differ
from it highlighted, then hits for an aryl sulfonamide SMARTS with the match highlighted.
[MP4 version](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/master/docs/media/search-demo.mp4).*

## Why this one

Other PubChem tools, MCP servers and hosted connectors included, forward questions to
PubChem's web API. That works for looking compounds up, but structure search through the
API is rate-limited, times out on generic queries and returns unscored samples. PubChem
Finder also keeps a local index:

- **Exact, scored similarity search** over every indexed compound (ECFP4 Tanimoto by
  default) in milliseconds, using [FPSim2](https://github.com/chembl/FPSim2), the engine
  behind ChEMBL's similarity search.
- **Local substructure search** with SMILES or SMARTS: a fingerprint screen, then an
  atom-by-atom match, so every hit is a real match.
- **Offline chemistry** with RDKit: descriptors, standardization, PAINS/Brenk/NIH alerts,
  QED, synthetic accessibility, and drawings that show what changed between analogues.
- **PubChem knowledge, cited:** synonyms and CAS numbers, cross-references, GHS
  classification, pharmacology, toxicity and bioassay summaries, each with its source.

No database server, no Docker: the index is a pair of files in your data directory.

## Use it from Claude

Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), which fetches
Python and everything else on first run.

**Claude Code:**

```bash
claude mcp add pubchem-finder -- uvx --python 3.14 pubchem-finder mcp
```

or as a plugin, which also works in Cowork:

```
/plugin install pubchem-finder --marketplace MysterionRise/pubchem-finder
```

**Claude Desktop** (Settings, Developer, Edit Config, then restart Claude):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pubchem-finder": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--python", "3.14", "pubchem-finder", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Then ask things like:

- "What is the molecular weight and XLogP of caffeine? Is it Lipinski-compliant?"
- "Is ibuprofen hazardous? What does its GHS label say? Cite the sources."
- "What are the main targets of celecoxib in PubChem bioassays?"
- "Show me the closest analogues of aspirin and highlight what changed."
- "Does this compound have any PAINS alerts

[![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/pubchem-finder.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/pubchem-finder/)
[![CI](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

<!-- mcp-name: io.github.MysterionRise/pubchem-finder -->

![A similarity search for aspirin and a SMARTS substructure search over 444,794 PubChem compounds, with the hits appearing and their key atoms highlighted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/master/docs/media/search-demo.gif)

from it highlighted, then hits for an aryl sulfonamide SMARTS with the match highlighted.

## Why this one

  atom-by-atom match, so every hit is a real match.
- **Offline chemistry** with RDKit: descriptors, standardization, PAINS/Brenk/NIH alerts,
  QED, synthetic accessibility, and drawings that show what changed between analogues.
- **PubChem knowledge, cited:** synonyms and CAS numbers, cross-references, GHS
  classification, pharmacology, toxicity and bioassay summaries, each with its source.

No database server, no Docker: the index is a pair of files in your data directory.

## Use it from Claude

Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), which fetches
Python and everything else on first run.

**Claude Code:**

```bash
claude mcp add pubchem-finder -- uvx --python 3.14 pubchem-finder mcp
```

or as a plugin, which also works in Cowork:

```
/plugin install pubchem-finder --marketplace MysterionRise/pubchem-finder
```

**Claude Desktop** (Settings, Developer, Edit Config, then restart Claude):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pubchem-finder": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--python", "3.14", "pubchem-finder", "mcp"]
    }

```

Then ask things like:

- "What is the molecular weight and XLogP of caffeine? Is it Lipinski-compliant?"
- "Is ibuprofen hazardous? What does its GHS label say? Cite the sources."
- "What are the main targets of celecoxib in PubChem bioassays?"
- "Show me the closest analogues of aspirin and highlight what changed."
- "Does this compound have any PAINS alerts? `O=C1C(=Cc2ccccc2)SC(=S)N1`"
- "Find the 20 compounds most similar to ibuprofen" or "Which indexed compounds contain an
  aryl sulfonamide? Draw a few with the group highlighted." (local search: the demo set of
  FDA-approved drugs until you build an index)

![Sulfonamide drugs with the aryl sulfonamide SMARTS match highlighted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/master/docs/images/sulfonamides-smarts.png)

*`draw_molecules` with `highlight="smarts"`: eight sulfonamide drugs with the match for
`[NX3][SX4](=O)(=O)c` highlighted, as Claude shows it inline.*

Local similarity and substructure search work from the first question: until you build
an index, they search a built-in demo set of 1,932 FDA-approved drugs (built in about a
second on first use) and say so. Build a PubChem index from the command line (below) and

`"env": {"PUBCHEM_FINDER_HOME": "/path"}` to the Claude Desktop entry, or
`--env PUBCHEM_FINDER_HOME=/path` to `claude mcp add`.

**Other MCP clients:** the server speaks standard MCP over stdio, so any client that runs
local MCP servers (Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, JetBrains IDEs, Codex CLI, LM Studio...)
can start it with the same command and arguments. It is listed in the
[MCP registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) as `io.github.MysterionRise/pubchem-finder`
